Fees f1,f2 must be nonnegative, paid from existing private income without borrowing, and sum to5*q. Each person must weakly prefer the project with its fee to no project. Find the surplus-maximising project without the individual approval constraints, decide whether it can be financed with both approvals, and find the largest project that can. Prove the result using a payment bound and an explicit financing rule.

Why can't perfect observational data alone determine a causal effect? Let all noises below be mutually independent standard normals. ModelA has X=U and Y=X/2+sqrt(3)*V/2. ModelB has X=(Z+U)/sqrt(2) and Y=(Z+V)/sqrt(2). Show that the observational joint distributions of(X,Y) are identical. Find E[Y|X=2] and Var(Y|X=2) in each model. Then replace the equation for X by the deterministic assignment X=2 while leaving the other equations and noise laws unchanged. Find the resulting mean and variance of Y in each model. Explain mathematically why no amount of observations of X and Y alone can distinguish these interventions.

Ich möchte die Auszahlungen durch ihre Quadratwurzeln ersetzen, weil die Reihenfolge gleich bleibt. Bleiben dadurch auch gemischte Gleichgewichte gleich? Zwei Spieler wählen A oder B. Die ursprünglichen Gewinne sind(4,1) bei(A,A), (1,4) bei(B,B) und(0,0) bei ungleichen Aktionen. Beide maximieren den Erwartungswert ihres angegebenen Gewinns. Finde die reinen und das vollständig gemischte Nash-Gleichgewicht. Ersetze dann nur die Gewinne des ersten Spielers durch die Quadratwurzel und löse erneut. Prüfe eine Antwort gegen einen Gegner, der A mit Wahrscheinlichkeit1/4 spielt, und erkläre, welche Transformationen Erwartungsnutzenvergleiche sicher erhalten.

Help me identify the market conduct from a cost experiment. Two firms have demands q1=2-p1+p2/2 and q2=2-p2+p1/2, with constant unknown unit costs c1,c2. Consider three candidate models: simultaneous price competition, firm1 publicly committing its price before firm2 responds, or firm2 committing first. Prices and quantities stay on a positive-demand interior branch. At baseline prices are(2,7/4). A small public unit tax added only to firm1's cost changes prices with exact derivatives(dp1/dt,dp2/dt)=(1/2,1/8). Determine the conduct model, recover both baseline costs and compute baseline quantities and profits. Derive the whole cost-to-price Jacobian under the identified model. Explain why the price snapshot alone would not identify conduct.

Comment répartir au moindre coût l'effort d'enquête et l'effort de sanction? Une entreprise gagne g>=0 si elle adopte une pratique. Une enquête arrive avec probabilité alpha, puis la sanction avec probabilité beta conditionnellement à l'enquête. Si elle est sanctionnée, elle perd tout le gain g et paie une amende fixe3; sinon elle garde g. L'autorité choisit alpha,beta dans[0,1] et supporte le coût alpha^2+4*beta^2. Une entreprise indifférente renonce à la pratique. Trouve le seuil de gain dissuadé pour alpha=beta=1/2. Trouve ensuite la politique de coût minimal dissuadant tous les gains jusqu'à9. Généralise à une borne h>=0 des gains: identifie le régime intérieur et le régime avec une probabilité saturée, sans essayer de nombreux couples.

Three independent observations are uniform on[0,theta], with unknown theta>0. The data are(1,2,4). Find the maximum-likelihood estimate and an unbiased minimum-variance estimate of theta. Derive the mean and variance of the sample maximum M. Within estimates k*M with constant k, find the one minimising squared-error risk and compare its risk with the unbiased estimate. Give an exact confidence interval with coverage7/8 of the form[M,c*M]. Explain why applying an ordinary score-based Cramer-Rao bound without checking support regularity can fail here. Use analytical distributions and moments, not simulation.

A public facility can have only integer size q in{0,1,2,3,4,5,6}. Benefits are U1(q)=9*q-q^2/2 and U2(q)=5*q-q^2/2. Real cost is2*q^2+F when q>0 and zero at q=0, with F>=0. Find the surplus-maximising size for every F without checking all seven choices. Compare the optimal positive integer size with the continuous positive-size optimum. At F=15, find all nonnegative fees financing the chosen facility while making each person weakly prefer it to no facility; assume sufficient private wealth to pay these fees. Explain why equating marginal benefit and marginal cost need not hold at the integer optimum.

I eliminated a weakly dominated action and found one outcome. Does that prove the original game had only one Nash equilibrium? Each player chooses A or B. Payoffs are(1,1) at(A,A), (1,0) at(A,B), (1,1) at(B,A), and(0,1) at(B,B). Find all Nash equilibria using p=P(player1 chooses A) and q=P(player2 chooses A). Compare eliminating player1's B first with eliminating player2's B first; call dominance weak only when at least one comparison is strict. Finally force each action to receive probability at least epsilon in(0,1/2), solve that constrained game, and take epsilon to zero. Explain what strict versus weak elimination preserves.

Pourquoi Copeland et Kramer-Simpson peuvent-ils répondre différemment alors qu'ils utilisent les mêmes duels? Douze électeurs ont les classements stricts suivants: cinq préfèrent A>B>C, quatre B>C>A et trois C>A>B. Calcule les voix de chaque comparaison, les scores de Copeland(victoires moins défaites), les scores Kramer-Simpson(minimum des voix reçues dans un duel), et les scores de Borda(2,1,0). Puis un électeur du premier groupe passe au deuxième classement. Compare les résultats et explique comment un score change de vainqueur sans qu'aucun sens de majorité change. Ne suppose pas qu'il existe un vainqueur de Condorcet.

A demand analyst forecasts a signed demand shock theta, with prior theta normal of mean0 and variance4. Reports are S1=theta+epsilon, S2=theta+epsilon+eta, S3=theta+nu. The noises are independent of theta and each other, with zero normal means and variances1,3,4 respectively. The observed reports are(2,8,4). Find the posterior mean and variance after S1, after(S1,S2), and after all three. Explain why the large second report adds no information once S1 is known. For a forecast a with loss(a-theta)^2, find the optimal forecast and conditional risk at each stage and the expected value of acquiring S3 after the first two reports. Use an innovation or covariance argument rather than counting every report as an independent measurement.

A mandatory public project of size G>=0 gives benefits U1=8*G-G^2/2 and U2=-2*G-G^2/2, and costs C=G^2/2. Private money is transferable and enters both utilities linearly; assume enough wealth for every stated payment. Find the efficient size and surplus. Can nonnegative household fees finance a positive project while making both households weakly better off than G=0? At the efficient size, characterise all balanced signed fees f1+f2=C that satisfy those participation constraints. Then find personalised unit prices pi such that each household maximises Ui(G)-pi*G at the efficient size and a producer maximising(p1+p2)*G-C(G) supplies it. Compute producer profit and show how an equal lump-sum rebate of that profit yields balanced fees and equal household gains. Rebates are fixed in each household's marginal decision.

How can I solve a large differentiated Cournot market without trying every possible set of active firms? There are n firms with qi>=0, prices pi=a-qi-gamma*sum(qj for j!=i), constant unit costs ci, and0<=gamma<=1. Derive a one-dimensional equilibrium equation and an exact method based on sorting costs. Give a uniqueness proof and explain why inactive high-cost firms need not be assigned negative quantities from an unconstrained linear solve. Apply the method to a=6, gamma=1/2 and costs(0,1,4,9), giving quantities, prices of the active goods and profits. Assume firms sell any chosen quantity at the stated inverse demand; the optimum can always choose zero.

Hilf mir, die Condorcet-Eigenschaft zu beweisen, statt viele Ranglisten auszuprobieren. Es gibt m>=3 Alternativen, eine ungerade Zahl2*r+1 von Wählern und strikt geordnete individuelle Präferenzen. Eine Alternative C schlägt jede andere im direkten Mehrheitsvergleich. Beweise, dass sowohl Copeland(Siege minus Niederlagen) als auch Kramer-Simpson(kleinste Stimmenzahl in einem direkten Vergleich) C eindeutig auswählen. Gib eine sichere untere Grenze für den jeweiligen Abstand zum nächstbesten Score und zeige, dass diese Grenzen scharf sind. Verwende zur Kontrolle fünf Wähler mit drei Ranglisten C>A>B>D und zwei Ranglisten A>C>B>D.

A survey samples two different households uniformly without replacement from four fixed incomes(0,2,4,6). Let X1 and X2 be the ordered sampled incomes, and estimate the population mean with their average. Derive its expectation and variance from the dependence between draws, rather than listing the possible samples. Compare with two draws with replacement. For an observed sample(2,6), estimate the variance of the sample mean using the usual unbiased sample variance and the finite-population correction. Prove the general covariance identity for n draws from N fixed values, distinguishing population variance with denominator N from the variance with denominator N-1.

Je ne comprends pas cet énoncé de monopole: p(q)=1-q, et C(q)=q+F pour q>0, avec F>=0. Fermer coûte0 et évite F; les quantités sont non négatives. Trouve l'issue viable et le surplus maximal sans inventer un coût marginal plus faible. Peut-on imposer une tarification au coût marginal ou au coût moyen avec une production positive? Pour F>0, prouve néanmoins que cette technologie est strictement sous-additive pour une production positive partagée entre plusieurs entreprises. Pourquoi cela ne suffit-il pas à établir l'existence d'un monopole naturel actif? L'utilité totale du consommateur est U(q)=q-q^2/2.

Le tableau du TD a des tirets lorsque les deux financeurs annoncent des qualités différentes. Peut-on calculer un équilibre sans préciser ces cases? Étudions une règle explicite: chacun choisit H,L ou N. Deux annonces de financement incompatibles annulent le projet et les paiements, donnant(0,0) pour(H,L) et(L,H). Les autres gains sont(H,H):(300,300), (H,N):(100,500), (N,H):(500,100), (L,L):(250,250), (L,N):(200,300), (N,L):(300,200), (N,N):(0,0). Trouve tous les équilibres purs et tous les équilibres symétriques mixtes, sans prétendre classer les autres équilibres asymétriques mixtes. Pour chaque mélange symétrique, donne les probabilités(H,L,N), le gain moyen individuel et le surplus collectif. Explique pourquoi cette règle de complétion peut changer les prédictions.

Two independent waiting times have exponential rate lambda>0, and the observed times are(2,4). Find the MLE and an unbiased estimate of lambda based on their sum S. Does the unbiased estimator have finite variance? Prove whether any estimator based on these two observations can be unbiased for every lambda and have finite variance. Compare with collecting exactly a third waiting time, observed as2, and derive the variance of the corresponding unbiased estimator. Finally use a Gamma prior for lambda with shape2 and rate1: find the posterior mean and variance after the original two observations, and explain why this regularised estimate has finite sampling second moments but is not a claim of unbiasedness.

Two households voluntarily contribute gi to a public good G=g1+g2. Their utilities are sqrt(xi*G), where xi=mi-gi is private consumption and0<=gi<=mi. Initial wealth is(14,2). A fixed lump-sum transfer t in[0,6] from household1 to household2 changes wealth to(14-t,2+t); the transfer is not conditional on contributions. Find the unique contribution equilibrium for every t, with all corner conditions. Compute public provision and utilities at t=0 and t=6. Explain exactly when redistribution reduces total provision and when it leaves provision unchanged. Use a common aggregate or best-response argument, not trial contribution pairs.

Help me separate efficient pollution control from compensation. A price-taking consumer has gross utility U(q)=2*q-q^2/2, the producer has cost C(q)=q^2/2, and a third party suffers damage E(q)=q. Compare the unregulated competitive equilibrium with a unit tax1 on production. Find consumer and producer prices, quantities, consumer surplus, producer surplus, tax revenue and the victim's utility change -E(q). The government redistributes all tax revenue through lump-sum transfers tC,tP,tV, positive when received; negative victim transfers are allowed, and there is enough money to make them. Characterise all transfers that make each of the three parties weakly better off than at the unregulated equilibrium. Can nonnegative rebates to everyone suffice? Find an equal-gain transfer scheme and explain why the tax alone does not make compensation automatic.

Two independent-looking failure reports give only marginal probabilities: P(A)=1/5 and P(B)=3/10. Independence is not assumed. Let the aggregate loss be L=indicator(A)+indicator(B). Find the sharp ranges of P(A and B), P(A or B), Var(L), and the correlation between the indicators. Give constructions attaining both endpoints. Compare the results with an independence calculation, and explain why knowing the mean aggregate loss does not identify the probability of losing two units.

Help me understand whether a refund promise can fix free riding. Two people each value a public project at100; its resource cost is150. In the original game, either may invest: two investors each pay75, one investor pays150 alone, and no investors means no project. Now replace this with an assurance contract: each may pledge75, and the project proceeds only if both pledge. If exactly one pledges, the project is cancelled, that pledge is fully refunded, and a committed outside sponsor pays that person a bonus b>=0. If neither pledges, nobody pays or receives anything. Utilities are monetary net gains. Find all Nash equilibria of the original game and of the contract at b=0 and b>0. Is there a smallest bonus that ensures a unique equilibrium? Explain the funding and credibility requirements and the equilibrium resource surplus.

How can I solve this without trying hundreds of tax rates? Abatement e>=0 gives social benefit B(e)=6*e-e^2. A firm incurs C(e;theta)=e^2/2+(2+theta)*e, where theta is -1 or1 with equal probabilities. The firm observes theta; the regulator chooses its policy before observing it. Compare an enforced fixed abatement quantity with a unit abatement subsidy t>=0. The firm maximises t*e-C(e;theta); subsidy funding is lump-sum, so payments are transfers. Find the globally optimal policy of each type, expected welfare and losses relative to a full-information planner. Include shutdown possibilities. Then derive the interior slope criterion for general benefit curvature b>0, cost curvature k>0 and a mean-zero marginal-cost shock of variance v, assuming all relevant choices remain positive.

Can you check my welfare estimate? True welfare is W(q)=4*q-q^2 for q>=0. I estimate the linear coefficient as aHat=4+epsilon, where epsilon is -1 or1 with equal probabilities, then choose qHat to maximise aHat*q-q^2. I report that maximised estimated welfare as the policy's performance. Find the expected reported welfare, the expected true welfare of the selected policy, and the optimism gap. Compare with the known-coefficient optimum. Would evaluating qHat using a second independent coefficient estimate4+epsilonPrime remove the bias? Generalise to W(q)=a*q-b*q^2/2 with b>0 and mean-zero estimation error of variance v, assuming estimated optima are always interior. Distinguish corrections targeting oracle welfare and deployed-policy welfare.

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi tirer au sort le payeur ne revient pas à partager les frais. Deux personnes ont chacune une richesse initiale de225. Un projet procure à chacune un gain monétaire de200 et coûte150. Leur utilité est la racine carrée de leur richesse finale. Dans le jeu volontaire, deux investisseurs paient75 chacun, un investisseur seul paie150, et sans investisseur le projet est abandonné. Compare les équilibres purs avec un contrat exécutoire qui répartit les frais non négatifs fA+fB=150. Trouve la répartition maximisant la somme des utilités. Une loterie équitable désigne alternativement A ou B comme seul payeur; compare sa richesse espérée, son utilité espérée, son équivalent certain et sa prime de risque avec le partage optimal. Les recommandations de cette loterie sont-elles obéies? Le partage optimal améliore-t-il nécessairement le sort de chacun par rapport à chaque équilibre pur?

Kannst du mir zeigen, warum eine Fusion die Gesamtwohlfahrt erhöhen kann, obwohl beide Preise steigen? Zwei differenzierte Produkte haben Nachfragen q1=8-2*p1+p2 und q2=8-2*p2+p1. Die Konsumenten haben quasilinearen Nutzen U(q1,q2)=8*(q1+q2)-(q1^2+q1*q2+q2^2)/3. Zwei getrennte Unternehmen setzen ihre Preise gleichzeitig; die Grenzkosten sind jeweils2. Nach einer Fusion wählt ein gemeinsamer Eigentümer beide Preise und senkt beide Grenzkosten auf2-epsilon, wobei0<=epsilon<=2. Es gibt keine Fixkosten. Bestimme die Preise, Mengen, Gewinne, Konsumentenrente und Ressourcenwohlfahrt vor und nach der Fusion. Finde die kleinste Kostensenkung, die den Wohlfahrtsverlust ausgleicht, und die kleinste, die Preiserhöhungen verhindert. Begründe auch, warum eine Aufgabe eines Produkts keine bessere Lösung ist.

Aide-moi à construire un exercice de Cournot avec des résultats simples, sans essayer des milliers de coefficients. Les demandes inverses sont p0=a-b*q0-g*q1 et p1=a-b*q1-g*q0, avec b>g>0. Les coûts sont C0=c0*q0 et C1=d1*q1^2, où c0>=0 et d1>0. Je veux un équilibre intérieur q0=q1=2, p0=p1=12, avec profits16 et20 respectivement. Quelles valeurs des paramètres ces objectifs imposent-ils, et lesquelles restent libres? Une observation supplémentaire dit que, si le produit1 disparaît, le monopole du produit0 pratique un prix14. Identifie alors tous les paramètres, vérifie l'équilibre et explique pourquoi l'observation du seul duopole ne suffisait pas.

I'm confused about tax incidence when a price cap creates a shortage. Consumers have demand D(pc)=max(0,10-pc), with a unit mass per unit of willingness to pay from0 to10. Competitive producers supply S(pp)=max(0,pp-2). A unit tax t>=0 creates pc-pp=t. First solve the unrestricted market. Now impose consumer price cap7: when the unrestricted price exceeds7, trade occurs at pc=7 and available supply determines quantity; for zero supply use the limiting quote7. Find the tax regimes, the revenue-maximising tax with and without the cap, and quantities. At t=3 compare welfare without the cap and with the cap under efficient rationing. Then find the sharp welfare range if any allocation among consumers willing to pay7 is allowed, and expected welfare under uniform random rationing. Treat tax revenue as a transfer and explain which incidence conclusions need a rationing rule.

Comment résoudre ce problème de bénévolat quand chacun connaît seulement son propre coût? Trois personnes choisissent simultanément de participer ou non. Le projet est réalisé dès qu'une personne participe, et procure à chacune un bénéfice1. Chaque participant paie son propre coût Ci, indépendamment du nombre de participants; les coûts sont indépendants et uniformes sur[0,1], et chacun observe seulement le sien. Trouve l'équilibre bayésien symétrique en stratégies de seuil, la probabilité d'échec, le coût total espéré et la somme des gains espérés. Compare avec un planificateur connaissant les trois coûts, qui peut désigner un seul participant. Explique la généralisation de l'équation de seuil à n personnes, sans supposer que tous les équilibres sont symétriques.

Help me check a sequential evidence rule, rather than just a fixed-sample test. Under the null, independent coin flips are fair. A competing model has head probability3/4. Start K0=1 and multiply capital by3/2 after a head and1/2 after a tail. Stop and reject as soon as K reaches3, with a maximum of four flips. Show why a threshold-crossing rule has null error probability at most1/3 even if the horizon is chosen adaptively. For this four-flip rule, compute the exact null rejection probability, the rejection probability under the competing model, and expected stopped capital under the null. Compare rejection on any crossing with checking only K4>=3. Explain which assumptions make the general error bound valid.

I thought a known final date always prevents cooperation. Help me check the missing assumption. Two players simultaneously choose C,D or R in a stage game. Payoffs are(4,4) at(C,C), (5,0) at(D,C), (0,5) at(C,D), (1,1) at(D,D), and(3,3) at(R,R); every other action pair gives(0,0). The stage game is played twice, with publicly observed first-period actions, independent private randomisation and total payoff u1+delta*u2 for0<=delta<=1. Find the stage Nash equilibria analytically and the lowest discount factor at which some subgame-perfect equilibrium can prescribe(C,C) in period1. Continuations may use pure or mixed stage equilibria. Construct such a strategy, prove its credibility after every history, and explain why backward induction does not force the same stage outcome after every history.

Can you check a symbolic cartel solution that gives a negative quantity? Two firms choose q0,q1>=0 and sell perfect substitutes at p=10-4*(q0+q1). Their costs are C0=c*q0 and C1=q1^2, with0<=c<=8. Compare the unique Cournot equilibrium with quantities maximising their joint profit. Derive the regimes analytically as c changes. At c=6, an unconstrained solver reports cartel quantities -5/2 and3 with total profit10: is that an economic optimum? At c=4 compute each firm's Cournot profit, the feasible cartel profits, and all transfers from firm1 to firm0 making both weakly willing to join. Assume such transfers are enforceable for this static participation comparison.

How can I identify hidden consumer types without searching over many possible mixtures? Each consumer has an unobserved purchase probability P taking exactly two distinct values in(0,1), both with positive population weights. Conditional on P, three purchase decisions are independent Bernoulli(P). We observe only K, the number of purchases, with population probabilities P(K=0)=P(K=3)=7/32 and P(K=1)=P(K=2)=9/32. Identify the two probabilities and their weights up to relabelling. Explain why one or two repeated decisions cannot identify this two-type model in general. Calculate Var(K), compare with a homogeneous Bernoulli model having the same mean, and predict a fourth purchase after observing three purchases. The fourth decision is independent of the earlier ones conditional on the same P.

Je ne sais pas si mon calcul de surplus a un sens. Je propose les demandes inverses p1=10-2*q1-q2 et p2=10-3*q1-2*q2, avec q1,q2>=0. Je veux les interpréter comme les utilités marginales d'un consommateur représentatif ayant un numéraire quasilinéaire et une utilité brute deux fois continûment différentiable. Cette interprétation est-elle possible? Vérifie en intégrant les prix de(0,0) à(1,1) selon les deux chemins rectangulaires. Calcule néanmoins l'équilibre de Cournot et les profits quand chaque firme a un coût unitaire2, en prenant les demandes comme fonctions de recettes. Puis remplace seulement le coefficient3 de p2 par1: reconstruis l'utilité normalisée à zéro en(0,0), vérifie sa concavité et calcule le surplus à(1,1). Explique ce qui distingue la résolution du jeu et la validité d'une mesure de bien-être.

Help me understand when a two-part tariff stops eliminating double marginalisation. An upstream monopolist has unit production cost2. It offers wholesale price w>=0 and upfront fee F>=0 to a risk-neutral monopolist retailer before demand is observed. Demand is max(0,a-p), with a=4 or8 equally likely. After accepting and paying F, the retailer observes a and chooses its selling price. Its outside option is0; acceptance depends on expected profit before a is observed, and it accepts at indifference. Statewise losses are permitted, with no additional financing constraints. First solve the upstream optimum with no fee cap. Then impose only the contractual restriction F<=1. Find the globally optimal contract, quantities in each state, expected profits of both firms, and expected resource welfare. Account for shutdown and participation regimes analytically.

How do I choose inventory if I trust the demand mean and variance, but not a full probability model? I pay1 per unit stocked, sell each unit for3 and cannot salvage leftovers. Demand D>=0 has mean4 and variance1. For stock q>=0, expected profit is3*E[min(D,q)]-q. Find the stock maximising worst-case expected profit over all demand distributions with these moments. Prove the result globally by constructing an admissible worst-case distribution and a saddle certificate, rather than searching many distributions. Contrast it with the optimal stock if demand were exactly3 or5 equally likely. Show that the robust stock is unique.

Can you explain why pricing my old shopping basket is not the same as maintaining my living standard? A consumer has utility sqrt(x*y), quantities x,y>=0, income8 and initial prices(1,1). Prices change to(4,1), with income unchanged. Find the optimal baskets and utility levels, the exact income needed to maintain original utility, compensating variation and equivalent variation. Define compensating variation as extra income at new prices restoring old utility, and equivalent variation as income removed at old prices to match new utility. Calculate the Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher price indices using the old and new optimal baskets. Generalise to relative price changes r1,r2>0, and determine whether Fisher is an exact cost-of-living index for this particular utility.

I'm trying to find one market-clearing price, but perhaps the price is not unique. Two consumers trade goods x,y with total supplies1,1. Consumer A owns(1,0) and has utility x+y. Consumer B owns(0,1) and has utility x+2*y. Quantities are nonnegative, both prices are positive, and normalise py=1,px=p. Find all competitive prices and allocations and check Pareto efficiency relative to the initial allocation. Then add a budget-balanced cash transfer of1/4 from A to B before purchases: incomes become p-1/4 and5/4, with p>=1/4 required for nonnegative income. Recompute prices, allocations and utilities. Explain why demand must be treated as a correspondence at a tie rather than assigning one arbitrary basket.

Help me separate a winning vote trade from an efficient policy. Three voters decide on projects X and Y. Utility gains are additive and monetary. Voter1 gets b from X and loses4 from Y; voter2 loses4 from X and gets b from Y; voter3 loses3 from each project. Assume b>0. Under sincere majority voting, a project or package passes only if at least two voters strictly prefer it to doing nothing. Compare separate ballots with a single X-and-Y package. Identify when the package passes yet reduces total welfare, and when budget-balanced transfers can make everybody weakly better off than doing nothing. At b=6, consider instead a nonbinding promise that voter2 will support X first and voter1 will support Y second; voter3 always votes no. Assume voter1 votes for X, voter2 votes for Y, and ties in personal payoffs are resolved against enactment. Is the reciprocal promise credible under backward induction?

How many separate taxes should I use if each one has a collection cost? There are ten independent identical competitive markets. In each, inverse demand is1-q and marginal production cost0. A unit tax t in[0,1] gives quantity1-t, gross revenue t*(1-t) and deadweight loss t^2/2. Each market with a positive tax also uses real collection resources1/100, paid from its revenue. The government must obtain net revenue1/2. Choose the number of taxed markets and their rates to minimise total deadweight loss plus collection costs. Untaxed markets incur no collection cost. Prove equal rates are optimal for any fixed number of active taxes, find the global integer optimum without enumerating all rate combinations, and check the government's net budget exactly.

Is the revenue-maximising tax also best when revenue finances something useful? A competitive private market has inverse demand10-q and constant marginal production cost2. A unit tax t in[0,8] is passed fully into the buyer price because supply is perfectly elastic. All revenue finances a public programme G=t*q, costing one resource unit per unit of G and giving gross social benefit B(G)=b*G, with b>0. There are no collection costs or other financing instruments. Find the welfare-maximising tax and programme for every b, compare them with the revenue-maximising policy, and derive the marginal social cost of raising one additional unit of revenue on the increasing Laffer branch. At b=2 give exact quantities, revenue, deadweight loss and net welfare gain. Explain why neither ignoring the public benefit nor counting tax revenue as an extra resource loss gives the right objective.

Help me interpret a job-training experiment without assuming everybody benefits. Binary potential employment outcomes are Y1 with training and Y0 without it. Random assignment is independent of both potential outcomes, and population employment probabilities are known exactly: P(Y1=1)=3/5 and P(Y0=1)=2/5. Only one potential outcome can be observed per person. Find the average treatment effect and sharp bounds on the fractions helped and harmed, and on the variance of individual treatment effects. Construct observationally indistinguishable populations attaining the bounds. A universal programme would impose utility cost1/10 on each person, and employment has utility value1: does its positive average net gain establish majority support? Finally impose the additional assumption Y1>=Y0 for every person and explain what becomes identified and what randomisation alone did not establish.

How can an aggregate pollution charge align incentives if individual emissions are not measured? Two firms choose emissions qi>=0 and each receives private benefit B(qi)=6*qi-qi^2/2. A third party suffers D(Q)=Q^2/2, where Q=q1+q2. Only Q is observed by the regulator. Compare no charge, a charge D(Q) imposed on each firm, and a charge D(Q)/2 on each firm. Find the Nash quantities and resource welfare and check which charge decentralises the social optimum. Now allow each firm's charge to be D(Q)-ri(qj), where its rebate depends only on the other's emissions, as a theoretical benchmark with those rebates observable. Can twice continuously differentiable rebates preserve incentives while making total charges equal D(Q) at every emission pair? Can constant rebates do so just at equilibrium? Construct an equilibrium-only example and explain the distinction. Transfers may be negative and there are enough reserves to honour any stated rebates.

Can you fit this economic response trend with the smallest guaranteed error rather than the smallest average squared error? Observations are(x,y)=(0,0),(1,0),(2,1),(3,1). Fit an unrestricted affine response yHat=a+b*x by minimising max absolute residual. Prove the minimum error and identify every minimising line without searching parameter grids. Compare with ordinary least squares: give coefficients, residuals, maximum error and sum of squared errors for both fits. Then suppose these observations and a future response at x=4 obey the same affine model with deterministic errors bounded by the smallest feasible bound. Find the sharp interval for that future response. This final bound is an assumption about future errors, not a statistical confidence interval.

Aide-moi à résoudre ce concours sans essayer beaucoup de niveaux d'effort. Deux agents choisissent simultanément ei>=0. Un sponsor attribue une récompense monétaire V>0: si e1+e2>0, la probabilité de victoire de i est ei/(e1+e2); si les deux efforts sont nuls, chacun gagne avec probabilité1/2. Le coût réel d'effort est ci*ei, avec ci>0. Les agents sont neutres au risque. Trouve tous les équilibres purs, justifie les conditions du premier ordre et traite les frontières. Pour V=12,c1=1,c2=2, donne efforts, probabilités, gains espérés et dépense réelle totale. Calcule le bien-être en incluant le sponsor, qui paie toujours V. Généralise la dépense d'effort et montre pourquoi son maximum, à V fixé, est atteint quand les coûts unitaires sont égaux.

Help me check whether a socially optimal redistribution would be voluntarily accepted. In an exchange economy, consumer A owns(3,1) and consumer B owns(2,4). Both have the stated cardinal utility U(x,y)=(x*y)^(1/4), quantities are nonnegative, and prices are positive. Find the competitive equilibrium, the Pareto-efficient allocations and the core relative to these endowments. Find the Bentham optimum, its supporting lump-sum transfers at prices(1,1), and whether it lies in the core. Then maximise the utility sum subject to voluntary participation, and decentralise that allocation. Use the given utility scale when adding utilities; do not replace it with a monotone transformation.

How should I spend a sampling budget when observations within a workplace share the same shock? Outcomes are Yij=mu+Ai+epsilonij. Workplace shocks Ai have mean0 and variance1; individual errors have mean0 and variance8. All workplace shocks and individual errors are mutually independent, except that people in the same workplace share its Ai. Sample N workplaces and m people per workplace, and estimate mu by the grand mean. Both N,m are positive integers. Visiting each workplace costs8 and observing each person costs1; total cost cannot exceed240. Prove the globally variance-minimising design without trying all integer pairs. Calculate its estimator variance, the variance from incorrectly treating sampled people as independent, the design effect and equivalent independent sample size. Compare with the feasible design N=24,m=2, then derive the interior continuous-allocation formula for general positive shock variance, individual variance and costs.

Can you solve this positive-externality exercise and also check how the subsidy is financed? A representative buyer has gross utility U(q)=q-q^2/2, a competitive producer has cost C(q)=q^2/2, and a third party receives external benefit E(q)=q/2. Quantity is nonnegative and money enters all utilities linearly. Find the unregulated equilibrium, resource-efficient quantity and welfare gain. Find the unit production subsidy implementing efficiency, buyer and seller prices, consumer and producer surplus, and subsidy expenditure. Would an equal unit purchase tax on the same traded quantity finance the subsidy while preserving efficiency? Finally give a nonnegative, budget-balanced lump-sum levy scheme on the three beneficiaries that funds the efficient subsidy and makes each weakly better off than without intervention.

Help me quantify how judgment errors change precaution incentives. An activity is always undertaken. Care costs1 and reduces accident probability from1/2 to1/5; real accident harm is10. Only an accident generates a claim. Causality is established with probability9/10, independently of the fault finding conditional on care and an accident. Under strict liability, established causality triggers damages F=10. Under negligence, damages also require a fault finding: a careless actor is mistakenly cleared with probability4/5, while a careful actor is mistakenly found at fault with probability1/5. Damages are transfers; litigation has no additional resource cost here. The actor is risk neutral and chooses care at indifference. Compare private decisions and social costs. Derive the general care conditions, the largest negligent false-clearance probability compatible with care in this numerical model, and the minimum damages restoring care under the specified errors. Explain when increasing damages cannot restore care.

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi un test très puissant peut quand même produire beaucoup de décisions erronées. Dans un modèle abstrait, un score S vaut0,1,2 ou3. Sous H0 ses probabilités sont(1/2,3/10,3/20,1/20); sous H1 elles sont(1/10,1/5,3/10,2/5). Une règle rejette H0 avec probabilité theta(S) dans[0,1]. Trouve la règle maximisant la puissance sous la contrainte de faux positifs P0(rejet)<=1/10, et prouve son optimalité sans essayer toutes les règles. Donne les sommets de la courbe puissance-taille optimale. Si la fréquence préalable de H1 vaut1/10, calcule P(H1|rejet) pour la règle optimale. Compare avec la règle minimisant le coût moyen quand un faux positif coûte1 et un faux négatif2. Ces probabilités et coûts sont des hypothèses du modèle, pas des données sur une population réelle.

Help me check a claim: “A negligence rule that induces efficient care must also induce efficient activity.” A risk-neutral actor chooses activity n>=0 and a common care decision for every unit. Gross benefit is B(n)=12*n-n^2. Without care, accident probability per unit is1/2; with care it is1/5 and care costs1 per unit. Each accident causes real harm10. Expected costs add across units. The victim is passive. Compare perfect strict liability with damages10 per accident and perfect negligence that imposes damages10 only if care is absent. All damages and taxes are transfers, courts cost nothing, and participation is optional. Find each private optimum and the social optimum, including care and activity. Quantify negligence's welfare loss. Can a constant tax per activity unit restore efficiency under negligence? Prove the decisions globally rather than just comparing care at one fixed activity.

Ich dachte, zwei Messungen würden den Messfehler automatisch beseitigen. Kannst du meine Rechnung prüfen? Alle Variablen sind zentriert. Ich beobachte Var(X1)=Var(X2)=6, Cov(X1,X2)=5, Cov(Y,X1)=Cov(Y,X2)=8 und Var(Y)=20. Das Modell lautet X1=X+U+E1, X2=X+U+E2 und Y=beta*X+eta. X,U,E1,E2,eta sind unabhängig mit endlichen Varianzen, Var(E1)=Var(E2)=1 und Var(X)>0. Der gemeinsame Messfehler U kann positive Varianz haben. Ich benutze X2 als Instrument für X1 und bekomme beta=8/5. Bestimme die naive OLS-Steigung, prüfe diese Instrumentenbehauptung und leite die scharfe identifizierte Menge für beta ab. Zeige durch passende latente Varianzen, dass jede zulässige Steigung wirklich dieselben beobachteten Momente erzeugt. Es handelt sich um ein hypothetisches statistisches Modell, nicht um Messdaten aus dem Kurs.

Comment puis-je passer de la technologie au coût marginal sans me perdre dans les multiplicateurs? Chaque entreprise produit q=(4/c)*x^(1/4)*y^(3/4), avec x,y>=0 et c=1/4. Les prix des facteurs sont initialement wx=1,wy=3. Trois entreprises identiques choisissent ensuite leurs quantités simultanément; le prix final est p=1-Q, Q étant la quantité totale. Il n'y a ni coût fixe ni capacité. Prouve le coût minimal de tout q>=0 et calcule les achats de facteurs, la quantité, le prix et le profit de chaque entreprise à l'équilibre. Le prix wx passe ensuite à16, tandis que wy reste3. Recalcule l'équilibre et explique pourquoi multiplier le prix d'un facteur par16 ne multiplie pas le coût marginal par16. Vérifie globalement la minimisation des dépenses, pas seulement les conditions du premier ordre.

Can you check this monopoly comparison? Two differentiated products have quasilinear gross utility U(q1,q2)=4*(q1+q2)-(2/3)*(q1^2+q1*q2+q2^2), with nonnegative quantities. Each product costs Ci(qi)=qi^2 to produce. Initially separate firms choose prices, with an interior demand system q1=2-p1+p2/2 and q2=2-p2+p1/2. A calculation says that when firm1 disappears, firm2 faces q2=2-p2, chooses price3/2 and earns1/2, less than its duopoly profit. Is that comparison consistent with the original preferences? Derive the separate-price equilibrium, the optimum when product1 is unavailable, and the optimum when one owner keeps both products. Compare prices, profits and total surplus in these three settings. Justify the relevant solutions globally and explain what setting p1=0 actually means.

How can I avoid the winner's curse here without trying hundreds of bids? Two risk-neutral bidders compete in a sealed-bid second-price auction for one item with common value V, equal to0 or12 with equal prior probabilities. Each sees a private signal H or L. Conditional on V=12, each signal is H with probability3/4; conditional on V=0, it is H with probability1/4. Signals are independent conditional on V. Bids are nonnegative, highest bid wins, the winner pays the other's bid, and tied bids split winning probability equally. There is no reserve and the item is always sold. I propose bidding E[V|own signal], namely9 after H and3 after L. Check this proposal. Construct a symmetric pure-strategy equilibrium with strictly higher bid after H, prove it against every unilateral bid, and compute expected seller revenue and total bidder profit. All distributions are hypothetical.

Je ne comprends pas ce résultat: la méthode delta donne une variance asymptotique nulle pour le bien-être, alors que ma politique estimée perd réellement du bien-être. Une politique est un ajustement signé t, autorisant aussi bien une taxe qu'une subvention. Son bien-être réel est W(t)=10-(t-mu)^2, avec mu inconnu. Pour choisir t, un analyste observe n variables indépendantes Zi de loi normale de moyenne mu et variance9, puis utilise tHat=la moyenne des Zi. Analyse la loi exacte de W(tHat), sa moyenne et sa variance. Explique pourquoi une approximation normale au taux sqrt(n) manque le phénomène et donne le bon taux et la loi limite. Calcule les résultats pour n=9, ainsi que la probabilité d'avoir W(tHat)>=6. Relie ensuite le calcul à W(t)=Wstar-(b/2)*(t-mu)^2 avec b>0 et variance individuelle sigma2. N'utilise pas de simulation.

Help me check the sign in this deterrence calculation. Relative to lawful conduct, an illegal exclusion gives a firm gain Delta=9 before enforcement. An investigation occurs with probability x and, conditional on investigation, conviction with probability y; take x=y=1/2. An unconvicted firm keeps the gain. If convicted, it pays a nonnegative fine F and returns a fraction gamma in[0,1] of the illicit gain. The firm is risk neutral and chooses lawful conduct at indifference; lawful conduct has incremental payoff0. Write the state payoffs and derive the minimum deterrent fine. Compare complete gain retention and complete disgorgement. A draft instead writes expected gain as Delta-x*y*(F-Delta) and obtains F=45. Can that draft describe any gamma in[0,1] under these assumptions? If gamma is unknown within this interval, what fine guarantees deterrence? Treat these as explicit hypothetical payoff conventions, not statements of current law.

My instrumental-variable estimate is a ratio, and its confidence interval looks strange. Can you explain it rigorously? Population moments A and B obey A=beta*B with B!=0. Their estimators Ahat and Bhat are independent normal variables with means A,B and known variances1,1. The observed values are Ahat=2 and Bhat=1. For a candidate beta, accept the moment restriction when |Ahat-beta*Bhat|<=2*sqrt(1+beta^2). Invert this exact normal test to obtain the confidence set for beta. Compare with the plug-in delta-method interval centred at Ahat/Bhat using the same critical value2. Give a geometric proof of the confidence set, explain its coverage and its disconnected shape, and decide whether beta=-1 and beta=-10 are included. Do not replace the set by a finite interval just because the observed denominator is positive.

Comment trouver le contrat le moins coûteux quand certaines rémunérations optimales devraient être négatives? Un salarié choisit un effort non observable e=0 ou1, de coût d'utilité e. Il reçoit une rémunération w>=0 selon un résultat L,M ou H, et son utilité est sqrt(w)-e. Sous effort1, les probabilités(L,M,H) sont(1/6,1/3,1/2); sous effort0, elles sont(1/2,1/3,1/6). Son option extérieure vaut r>=0. L'employeur neutre au risque veut implémenter effort1 au coût salarial moyen minimal. Le salarié accepte et fournit effort1 aux indifférences correspondantes. Trouve le contrat optimal pour tout r>=0, ses seuils de régime, son coût attendu et la rente au-dessus de l'option extérieure. Prouve globalement l'optimalité avec les contraintes de participation, d'incitation et de non-négativité; calcule aussi les salaires pour r=0,1 et2. Ces paramètres sont un complément hypothétique au cours d'information imparfaite.

Can a transfer sustain this cartel when the public signal makes mistakes? Two firms choose q0,q1>=0 with p=40-q0-q1, costs C0=16*q0 and C1=q1^2. The cooperative quantities maximise joint operating profit; punishment is permanent one-shot Cournot. In each cooperative period, a nonnegative enforceable transfer T from firm1 to firm0 is paid BEFORE quantities are chosen; it is not cancelled by a current deviation or signal. At period end a public bad signal arrives with probability alpha=1/5 if both comply and beta=1/2 if exactly one deviates to any different quantity. A bad signal triggers punishment from next period; a good signal keeps cooperation. Signals are conditionally independent over time given behaviour. Punishment periods have no transfer. Both firms discount by delta in[0,1). Find operating profits under cooperation, punishment and best unilateral deviations. Derive all sustainable transfers and the smallest delta; give the transfer interval at delta=19/20. Prove the public incentives and explain why the difference beta-alpha, not beta alone, measures the signal's disciplinary power.

Help me understand why my experiment may not answer the rollout question. People live in pairs. A person's expected outcome is mu+tau*Z+gamma*Zneighbor, where own treatment Z and neighbour treatment Zneighbor are0 or1. The common baseline mu is unknown but lies in[0,1]; errors have conditional mean0. In every experimental pair exactly one person is treated, chosen by a fair coin. The population mean among treated people is3 and among untreated people is1. Can I interpret the treated-minus-untreated difference as the effect per person of treating everyone rather than nobody? Find the identified treatment and spillover combinations, and sharp bounds on the rollout effect. Explain the rank problem algebraically. A second randomised experiment adds pairs with neither person treated and finds mean1/2 there; what does this identify? Treatment costs5/2 per person, and outcomes are measured in transferable welfare units. Is full rollout better than no treatment before and after that extra information? State the assumptions needed for the comparison.

No entiendo cómo un impuesto de1/4 puede subir el precio al consumidor en1/2. ¿Puedes demostrarlo sin buscar cantidades una por una? Un monopolista enfrenta demanda inversa p(q)=1/sqrt(q) para q>0, con ingreso0 si q=0. Su coste real es c*q, donde c=1/4. Un impuesto por unidad t se paga al gobierno y el beneficio es p(q)*q-(c+t)*q. Se permite una subvención t<0, pero c+t debe ser positivo. Calcula el equilibrio sin impuesto y con t=1/4, la transmisión del impuesto, los excedentes y la recaudación. Encuentra el impuesto no negativo que maximiza la recaudación y la intervención que maximiza el bienestar real cuando se admiten subvenciones. El gobierno puede financiar o devolver los pagos mediante transferencias de suma fija; no hay otro coste fiscal. Usa beneficio bruto del consumidor U(q)=2*sqrt(q).

How can adding firms fail to eliminate market power if the market size is held fixed? Consider n>=1 differentiated products with quasilinear gross utility U=a*Q-[n*sum(qi^2)+m*Q^2]/[2*(1+m)], where Q=sum(qi),qi>=0,m>=0 and a>c>=0. Every firm has cost c*qi and chooses quantity simultaneously. Derive the unique Cournot equilibrium and its aggregate welfare. Compare it with efficient production and joint-profit maximisation. Analyse n tending to infinity with m fixed, and m tending to infinity with n fixed. Evaluate quantities, price, per-firm profit and the welfare efficiency ratio at a=4,c=1,n=4,m=10. Explain exactly what this normalisation holds fixed and why the standard homogeneous Cournot limit cannot be imported blindly.

Je pensais qu'un monopole supprimant un produit et réduisant la quantité faisait forcément baisser le bien-être. Peux-tu vérifier cette intuition dans le même modèle de préférences? Le bénéfice brut est U(q1,q2)=a*(q1+q2)-q1^2-q2^2-(1/2)*q1*q2, avec a>=0 et quantités non négatives. Les coûts sont C1=q1,C2=q2/2. Compare deux entreprises choisissant leurs quantités simultanément avec un propriétaire commun maximisant le profit des deux produits. Dérive les régimes de produits actifs en fonction de a, sans accepter des quantités négatives. Puis, à a=9/8, calcule quantités, prix des produits effectivement vendus, profits et bien-être réel. Le propriétaire commun réduit-il le nombre de produits et la quantité totale? Son bien-être est-il nécessairement inférieur ici? Précise la différence entre ce contre-exemple et une recommandation générale de fusion.

I changed quantities to prices and got the same equilibrium by differentiating p=a-Q. Where did I go wrong? There are n>=2 products with utility U=a*Q-[n*sum(qi^2)+m*Q^2]/[2*(1+m)],qi>=0,m>=0,a>c>=0. Firms have constant marginal cost c and now choose nonnegative prices simultaneously. Consumers maximise U-sum(pi*qi). Derive a symmetric price equilibrium, including the correct own-price derivative, and verify it against global unilateral price deviations. Compare aggregate output with the quantity-game equilibrium Q_C=n*(1+m)*(a-c)/[n*(2+m)+m]. Analyse the limits n tending to infinity at fixed m and m tending to infinity at fixed n. Give prices, quantities, per-firm profit and welfare ratio for a=4,c=1,n=4,m=10. Explain why differentiating the symmetric aggregate relation is not the unilateral pricing problem.

Help me check whether firms should commit to prices or quantities. Gross utility is U=4*(q1+q2)-(q1^2+q2^2)-d*q1*q2, with qi>=0 and marginal cost1 for both products. Compare d=1 (substitutes) with d=-1 (complements). First each firm publicly chooses a binding price or quantity commitment. They then choose the committed variables simultaneously. If both choose quantities, market-clearing prices come from marginal utility. If both choose prices, consumers maximise U minus expenditure. In a mixed game, the quantity product's announced output is sold at its marginal-utility price, while demand for the price product adjusts, including its zero-quantity boundary. Derive continuation equilibria and each firm's profit for both homogeneous commitment pairs and a mixed pair. Determine the unique commitment equilibrium in each case. Prove the relevant continuation best responses globally. Is comparing the profits under two price commitments with those under two quantity commitments enough to establish commitment dominance?

How can a valid random encouragement produce a negative IV estimate when treatment helps every person? Let Z be randomly assigned, independent of all potential variables, with treatment choices D(0),D(1). Outcomes satisfy Y=Y(0)+D*(Y(1)-Y(0)), so encouragement has no direct effect. In this hypothetical population, compliers have probability1/2 and(D(0),D(1))=(0,1), defiers probability1/4 and choices(1,0), always-takers probability1/8 and choices(1,1), and never-takers probability1/8 and choices(0,0). Everyone has Y(0)=0. Treatment effects are2 for compliers,6 for defiers and4 for the other two groups. Compute the first stage, outcome contrast, Wald ratio and population average treatment effect. Derive the signed-weight interpretation and explain why a positive first stage does not prove monotonicity. Then forget the supplied latent table: retain only the observed conditional treatment and outcome means, the stated randomisation/exclusion assumptions, Y(0)=0 and treatment effects in[0,6]. Prove a sharp lower bound on the defier fraction by constructing a population attaining it and matching all four means. Do not search through possible populations.

Comment un candidat peut-il perdre parce que des électeurs le remontent dans leur classement? On utilise un scrutin uninominal à deux tours: les deux premiers en nombre de premières places passent au second tour, puis chacun vote sincèrement pour son préféré entre les finalistes. Une égalité de premières places entre B et C est résolue en faveur de B; une égalité au second tour est résolue en faveur de A. Il y a7 électeurs A>B>C,8 électeurs B>C>A et6 électeurs C>A>B. Parmi les8 du deuxième groupe, x électeurs remplacent leur classement par A>B>C, avec x entier dans[0,8]. Ils remontent A et conservent leur comparaison B>C; rien d'autre ne change. Détermine le gagnant en fonction de x par des seuils, sans recalculer les neuf profils séparément. Calcule les résultats détaillés pour x=0 et x=3, puis vérifie les comparaisons majoritaires par paire et la présence d'un vainqueur de Condorcet. Cela contredit-il l'affirmation qu'un perdant de Condorcet ne peut pas gagner un second tour sincère?

Should I use majority voting to combine three expert reports? A project is good or bad. Expert1 reports the true state with probability9/10, while experts2 and3 each do so with probability2/3. Errors are symmetric across states and reports are independent conditional on the state. Approving a bad project or rejecting a good one costs1; correct decisions cost0. At posterior ties, reject. First use a good-project prior1/2: derive the Bayes decision without listing all eight report combinations and compare its error risk with ordinary majority voting. Is it worth paying for the two weaker reports after observing expert1? Repeat the Bayes decision and value calculation when the good-project prior is1/10. Finally, under prior1/2 suppose expert3 simply copies expert2 instead of being conditionally independent; keep their marginal accuracies unchanged. Derive majority risk and the posterior after three good reports, contrasting it with the posterior obtained by falsely assuming independence. These are hypothetical report accuracies, not measured expert performance.

Can you help me solve this voting example and check a hidden turnout assumption? Twenty-one voters have fixed rankings:10 prefer A>B>C,6 prefer B>C>A and5 prefer C>B>A. Compare sincere plurality voting, sincere two-round voting with the two largest first-place totals advancing, all pairwise majority comparisons, and Borda scores(2 for first,1 for second,0 for last). All21 vote in the first round. In a possible A-B runoff, exactly k of the5 C>B>A voters abstain, with integer0<=k<=5; everyone else votes sincerely. A second-round tie favours B. Find the smallest k making A win without trying each turnout count. Does that outcome contradict the statement that a Condorcet loser cannot win a sincere runoff? Keep the distinction between the full electorate and the people actually voting.

Are employer payroll taxes and worker consumption taxes equivalent once a wage floor binds? Use this hypothetical labour market. The producer-good price is1. Workers supply one unit each, with reservation cost r uniformly distributed at density1 on[0,12]; a worker works if its consumption purchasing power omega is at least r. A firm gets real output benefit B(L)=12*L-L^2/2, so labour demand at employer cost C is max(0,12-C). Gross contractual wage w excludes employer contributions. With employer rate e, employee rate s, income-tax rate i on post-contribution income, and a tax v only on wage-financed worker consumption, C=(1+e)*w and omega=(1-s)*(1-i)*w/(1+v). Revenue is a transfer; no other fiscal costs or taxed spending are included. Compare policy E:(e,s,i,v)=(1,0,0,0) with policy V:(0,0,0,1). First clear the flexible-wage market. Then impose w>=5, employment equal to the smaller of labour supply and demand at the binding wage. Compare wages, employment, involuntary unemployment and receipts. Under E, bound real welfare over all allocations of jobs among willing workers, and calculate welfare under uniform random rationing. Explain the assumption on which tax equivalence depends.

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi déduire les intérêts pourrait modifier à la fois l'endettement et l'investissement. Peux-tu le montrer sans tester une multitude de combinaisons? Dans ce modèle hypothétique, une entreprise choisit un capital K>=0 et une dette D comprise entre0 et K; le reste est financé par fonds propres. Son bénéfice d'exploitation réel est F(K)=12*K-K^2/2. Dette et fonds propres ont le même coût d'opportunité unitaire r=2. L'endettement entraîne en plus un coût réel non déductible H(K,D)=2*D^2/K pour K>0, prolongé par H(0,0)=0. Le taux d'impôt sur les sociétés est tau dans[0,1]. Seuls les intérêts de la dette sont déductibles: T=tau*(F(K)-2*D), sans plafonnement ni restriction de signe; le profit après impôt et après rémunération des deux sources de financement est Pi=F(K)-2*K-H(K,D)-T. Les recettes fiscales sont des transferts. Pour tau=1/2, trouve K,D,T,Pi et le surplus réel W=F(K)-2*K-H(K,D). Décompose la perte de surplus par rapport au premier optimum sans impôt ni dette. Détermine aussi les choix pour tout tau et le seuil exact d'arrêt de l'investissement. Compare avec un impôt alternatif déduisant le coût normal de tout le capital, Tn=tau*(F(K)-2*K), à tau=1/2. Toutes les conventions fiscales sont celles du modèle, pas une description d'une législation actuelle.

Help me decide whether a safe action is irrational without trying hundreds of mixtures. An economic decision maker chooses U,V,W or Z while an opponent chooses L,M or R. Only the decision maker's payoffs are specified: U gives(6,0,2), V gives(0,4,1), W gives(1,2,5), and Z gives(a,a,a), where a>=0. Find the mixture of U,V,W that maximises its worst payoff across the three opponent actions, prove global optimality and uniqueness, and give the largest guaranteed gain over Z. Classify when Z is strictly dominated by a pure action, strictly dominated by a mixture, or a best response to some belief about the opponent. Treat the equality case carefully: weak domination means at least one strictly better payoff and no worse payoff. At a=2, provide both a dominance certificate and an independent upper bound. Can the opponent's belief certificate establish a Nash equilibrium when the opponent's payoffs are missing?

My lecture says cooperation unravels when a repeated game has a known final period. Is the known endpoint enough, or does the unique stage-equilibrium assumption matter? Consider this hypothetical symmetric stage game with actions C,D,P. Payoffs are(C,C):(4,4), (D,C):(5,0), (C,D):(0,5), (D,D):(1,1), and(P,P):(3,3). Every other pair involving P gives(0,0). The game lasts a publicly known T>=2 periods, with perfect observation and common discount factor delta in[0,1]; current payoffs plus discounted future payoffs are maximised. There are no external transfers or committed enforcement contracts. Study this complete strategy: after a history consisting only of(C,C), play C before the terminal period and P in the terminal period; after any other observed action pair, play D in every remaining period. Find exactly when this strategy is subgame perfect, checking every history. Derive the compliance-minus-best-deviation gain with m>=2 periods remaining and explain which cooperative history is binding. Evaluate the path payoff and every distinct remaining-horizon incentive at T=4,delta=3/4. Compare with removing P, and state whether you have classified all repeated-game equilibria.

I thought giving pollution permits away differently only redistributes money. Does that remain true if one firm influences the permit price? Use this explicitly specified trading game. Each of two firms emits5 before abatement; ai lies in[0,5], with real costs C1=a1^2/2 and C2=2*a2^2. Total permits are4. Firm1 receives omega in[0,4], and firm2 receives4-omega. There is no banking, no unused permits, and all transactions use a single price p. In the competitive benchmark both firms take p as given. In the strategic game firm1 chooses its abatement a1 anticipating the price-taking firm's response a2=p/4, the clearing identity a1+a2=6, and net permit sales s=omega-(5-a1). Firm1 may sell or buy: s can be negative. Its private objective is p*s-C1, with fixed baseline operating returns omitted. Firm2 takes the price as given and pays for its net purchases. Restrict the leader to feasible a1 in[1,5], so the cap clears with admissible fringe abatement. Derive the competitive benchmark and the strategic outcome for every omega. At omega=4 and omega=2 compute price, abatement, trading and total real cost; at omega=4 also calculate both firms' net private compliance costs. Prove the strategic allocation's real cost loss, identify the free allocation restoring efficiency, and explain why an unchanged emissions cap does not imply unchanged welfare.

Je ne comprends pas le dernier objectif du cours: recettes des permis plus bénéfice environnemental, est-ce vraiment le surplus collectif? Étudions le modèle suivant. Deux entreprises émettent4 unités chacune avant abattement. Elles choisissent k1,k2 dans[0,4], avec coûts réels C1=k1^2 et C2=3*k2^2. L'abattement total est K=k1+k2, les émissions Q=8-K, et le bénéfice environnemental B(K)=16*K-K^2. Les bénéfices de production sont fixes et omis. Le surplus réel est W=B(K)-C1-C2; les paiements de permis sont des transferts. Trouve l'optimum social et le prix concurrentiel des permis qui le met en œuvre. Compare avec une obligation uniforme k1=k2, d'abord au même K socialement optimal, puis en choisissant son meilleur K. Ensuite, un office choisit p dans[0,24]. Chaque entreprise prend p comme donné et minimise son coût d'abattement plus p fois ses émissions; l'office vend exactement Q(p) permis et maximise O(p)=p*Q(p)+B(K(p)), sans soustraire les coûts privés. Calcule son optimum global, les abattements, émissions, recettes et surplus réel associés. Montre où la contrainte d'abattement change les formules et explique si les recettes peuvent être ajoutées au surplus sans soustraire les paiements des entreprises. Il s'agit d'un modèle hypothétique, pas de règles actuelles de marché.

Help me check my standard error: I treated six panel observations as independent. In a hypothetical model there are three groups with two observations each, Ygi=beta*xgi+Ag+epsilon_gi. The regressor is fixed, with group pairs(-3,-1),(0,2),(1,1). There is no intercept or other regressor in the fitted model. Group shocks have mean0 and variance3; individual errors have mean0 and variance1. All these shocks are mutually independent across groups and individuals. No Gaussian assumption is needed. The observed Y pairs are(-4,-1),(1,4),(3,2). Derive the OLS estimator and its actual variance, compare with the variance obtained by wrongly using identity error covariance, and construct the unique minimum-variance linear unbiased estimator using known covariance. Avoid inverting a six-by-six matrix blindly: decompose the regressor into within-group deviations and repeated group means. Compute the within-only estimator, its variance and its relation to GLS. Prove the global linear-unbiased optimality of GLS. Replace Var(Ag)=3 by t>=0 and examine t=0 and t tending to infinity. Finally, if Ag are instead arbitrary unknown group constants, which displayed estimator remains unbiased conditional on those constants, and why do the random-effects GLS assumptions matter?

How can a bargaining model have a best achievable limit but no equilibrium? Two risk-neutral players divide a unit surplus. Player1 offers a share x in[0,1] to player2 and keeps1-x if player2 accepts; rejection gives both0. Player2 observes x. Compare acceptance at indifference with a stipulated behavioural rule rejecting at indifference, while accepting every strictly positive offer. Under the first rule, find the subgame-perfect outcome. Under the second, prove that no subgame-perfect equilibrium respecting that rule exists, even if player1 randomises over offers. If no tie rule is imposed, let player2 accept x=0 with probability rho and show which rho can occur in a subgame-perfect equilibrium. Now restrict offers to the grid{0,1/N,...,1}, with integer N>=2, under rejection at zero. Derive its equilibrium analytically and assess the limit as N grows. Finally, define an epsilon-subgame-perfect profile to allow no unilateral improvement greater than epsilon in any subgame, with epsilon in(0,1). Characterise the pure accepted offers satisfying this condition under rejection at zero. Distinguish a supremum, a maximum, and convergence of grid outcomes to an equilibrium of the continuous game.

Aide-moi à comprendre pourquoi un financement adopté à la majorité peut être injuste sans être optimal pour la somme des utilités. Trois individus A,B,C ont chacun une richesse initiale20 et une utilité sqrt(richesse finale). Un bien public indivisible coûte12 et procure des gains monétaires9,9,5 respectivement. S'il est produit, les contributions obligatoires ti sont non négatives, leur somme vaut12 et les richesses finales sont20+Gi-ti. Sans projet, chacun conserve20. Un individu vote oui s'il est au moins aussi bien que sans projet; les indifférences votent oui. A et B contrôlent ensemble la proposition soumise à un référendum à majorité simple. Ils choisissent le financement maximisant la somme de leurs propres utilités, puis votent selon la règle donnée. Trouve leur proposition et les votes; compare avec le financement maximisant la somme des trois utilités et vérifie si ce dernier passe même avec un veto individuel. Caractérise aussi tous les financements non négatifs acceptables à l'unanimité. Puis remplace seulement le gain de C par h dans[0,8] et dérive le financement utilitariste pour tout h, en gardant la contrainte ti>=0. Ces richesses et l'utilité racine carrée sont des hypothèses numériques ajoutées au problème du cours.

The course gives inequalities between voter groups instead of exact counts. How can I solve every voting rule without trying group sizes one by one? Three groups have positive integer sizes n1,n2,n3 with n2<n3<2*n1/3 and n2+n3>n1. Their rankings are respectively A>B>C, B>A>C and C>B>A. Voting is sincere, with everyone participating. Compare one-round plurality, a top-two runoff, the Condorcet winner and loser, and every sequential pairwise elimination agenda. Also apply Borda scores(2,1,0), Copeland scores equal to the number of pairwise wins, and Simpson-Kramer scores equal to the smallest number of supporters obtained in a pairwise contest. Finally suppose utilities are(3,1,0) in ranking order and maximise their sum, the Bentham criterion. Prove all winners directly from the inequalities. Check the admissible instance(n1,n2,n3)=(12,6,7), giving pairwise vote counts, Borda, Copeland, Simpson-Kramer and utility-sum scores. Explain why an ordinal majority winner need not maximise this explicitly supplied cardinal welfare measure.

Can you map the voting regions without sampling hundreds of possible tax bills? A public project costs12 and gives monetary gains(9,9,5) to A,B,C. Each has sufficiently large initial wealth and a strictly increasing utility function. Taxes are nonnegative and balance the cost: tA+tB+tC=12. A voter approves if the project leaves it at least as well off as no project; indifference counts as approval. Describe the feasible budget triangle in the(tA,tB) plane and every region with zero, one, two or three yes votes, including who rejects. Find the vertices and area of the unanimity region, and check equal sharing. As an explicit additional statistical experiment, draw a proposal uniformly by area from that budget triangle. Compute the probability of each vote count, each individual rejection probability and the expected yes count; decide whether individual approval indicators are independent. Finally prove the general condition under which every nonnegative financing proposal passes a majority vote for three gains Gi in[0,P], and apply the course's intervals GA=GB in(2*P/3,P) and GC in(P/3,2*P/3). No claim is made that real political proposals are uniformly drawn.

Please check this correction before I learn the wrong profit comparison. Two monopolists sell unrelated goods with inverse demands pi=1-qi, qi>=0. Their net real costs are Ci=(1/3)*qi+alpha*qj, with alpha in[-1/3,1/3]. The signed cross-cost represents harm for alpha>0 or an external real benefit for alpha<0. It remains in the firm's account when its own output is zero; there is no exit option removing it. Each firm first chooses output independently, then consider joint profit maximisation under unchanged primitives. Consumers have gross benefits Ui=qi-qi^2/2. Derive quantities, prices, total producer profit, total consumer surplus and resource welfare before and after coordination, and the efficient allocation, as functions of alpha. A draft claims (2/3-alpha)^2/2 > (2/3)*(2/3-2*alpha)/4 if and only if alpha!=0. Audit that statement and repair the comparison of total profits. Prove the merger-welfare sign over the entire stipulated interval and check both endpoints. Explain why a profit gain or a higher price alone is insufficient to decide welfare, and why the parameter restriction matters.

Help me interpret the course's maximum bargaining transfer without confusing it with a tax rebate. Consumer benefit is U(q)=2*q-q^2/2, production cost is C(q)=q^2/2, and victim damage is D(q)=q. Restrict the activity to q in[0,1]. The consumer and producer form a binding transferable-utility coalition M with payoff S(q)=U(q)-C(q); internal transfers are unrestricted and no separate market-clearing price is imposed on their negotiated quantity. The victim's payoff before transfers is -q. Bargaining is informed and enforceable. In regime A, M owns the right to choose activity; disagreement is its private optimum. In regime B, the victim owns the right to prohibit activity; disagreement is q=0. Find the efficient quantity and all individually rational net transfers implementing it in each regime, stating the payer. Transfers are accepted at indifference. Then impose only a cash-payment cap b in[0,1] on the party paying to change the disagreement outcome, with borrowing or future payments unavailable. In each regime choose q to maximise real joint surplus subject to both parties' disagreement participation constraints and this cap. Derive the constrained quantity and transfer range for every b. Evaluate b=1/16, and identify the budget thresholds at which efficiency becomes feasible. Explain which additional coalition and liquidity assumptions make this a precise extension of the source problem, and why property-right invariance can fail under the payment cap.

Não percebo por que um projeto que cria riqueza pode tornar inviável a divisão igual. Duas pessoas podem conservar os capitais(C1,C2) ou investi-los num projeto com produção certa Y. A produção substitui os capitais investidos, não é somada novamente a eles. As receitas finais R1,R2 são não negativas, com R1+R2<=Y; permitimos descartar produção. Cada pessoa tem utilidade sqrt(Ri), e só participa se não ficar pior do que conservando o seu capital. Uma melhoria de Pareto exige ainda que pelo menos uma fique estritamente melhor. Para Y=250, analisa primeiro(C1,C2)=(100,50) e depois(150,50). Calcula a riqueza criada, toda a região de participação, a sua fronteira eficiente, e o máximo da soma das utilidades com e sem participação obrigatória. Generaliza a C1>=C2>0 e a qualquer Y>=0: identifica quando o projeto admite uma melhoria de Pareto e quando a divisão igual é implementável. Prova os resultados sem testar repartições sucessivas.

Help me check my argument: if two people keep exactly the same preferences after an increasing change of utility units, surely the best social allocation cannot change? They share 100 euros, with R1,R2>=0 and R1+R2<=100. Both initially have U(R)=sqrt(1+R)-1. I replace it for both by V(R)=(1+R)^2-1, an increasing transformation of U. Rawls maximises the smaller utility; Bentham maximises the sum. Determine the efficient allocations and both criteria's complete sets of optima before and after the transformation, including the optimum utility values. Derive the slope and curvature of the utility frontier for a general twice differentiable common U with U'>0, and explain what strict concavity, strict convexity and affine utility imply. Give the exact frontier equations and midpoint curvature for these two utilities. Is “no inflection point” by itself enough to assert a unique Bentham optimum? I want an analytic argument, not a scan over possible allocations.

Wie kann ich das lösen, ohne alle möglichen Kostenaufteilungen auszuprobieren? Zwei Personen A und B besitzen jeweils225. Ein öffentliches Projekt kostet150 und erhöht ihre Geldvermögen vor Finanzierung um200 beziehungsweise100. Eine Institution produziert das Projekt und wählt nichtnegative Beiträge fA+fB=150; Kredite sind unnötig, da jeder Beitrag höchstens150 beträgt. Die Endvermögen sind zA=425-fA und zB=325-fB. Ohne Projekt besitzt jeder225. Bestimme alle optimalen Beiträge für Bentham zunächst mit gemeinsamer Nutzenfunktion sqrt(z), dann mit z^2, sowie für Rawls mit beiden Funktionen. Berechne die Endvermögen und Zielfunktionswerte. Wiederhole Bentham unter freiwilliger Teilnahme: Niemand darf schlechter als ohne Projekt stehen. Erkläre, ob die jeweils unbeschränkte Lösung freiwillig durchsetzbar ist. Beweise mit einem allgemeinen Argument für gemeinsame streng konkave beziehungsweise streng konvexe, steigende Nutzenfunktionen, welche Aufteilungen hier optimal sind. Ein Vergleich nur einiger Testpunkte reicht nicht.

In the public-goods exercise, I get the same investment choices whether people move together or one after the other. Can you check what I missed? I also used the proposed investment advantage Gi-150-75*p when the other invests with probability p; please check that formula. Two people choose I(invest) or N(abstain). If both invest, each pays75; a lone investor pays150; with neither investing there is no project. Whenever someone invests, both receive their respective monetary benefits GA,GB. Utilities are benefit minus own payment, or0 without the project. Analyse the source cases(GA,GB)=(100,100),(200,200),(200,100). Find all simultaneous Nash equilibria, including mixed equilibria, and all subgame-perfect equilibria when A moves first and B observes A. State the provision probabilities and expected real social surplus. Explain whether reversing the order changes the asymmetric case. Then analyse the additional boundary GA=GB=150: characterise all simultaneous mixed equilibria and all behavioural subgame-perfect equilibria, allowing arbitrary mixing when indifferent. Give the sequential off-path actions too. Use payoff differences and backward induction rather than a strategy-profile search.

Je ne comprends pas comment on peut dire qu'un équilibre devient «plus probable» parce qu'un bien privé est substituable au bien public. Peux-tu distinguer ce qui est démontré de ce qui dépend d'une règle de sélection? Voici un modèle explicite inspiré de l'exercice de qualité. Deux personnes ont chacune1000 unités de bien privé. Elles choisissent H ou L dans un contrat de financement conditionnel. Si elles choisissent toutes deux H, la qualité publique est Q=2 et chacune paie200. Si elles choisissent toutes deux L, Q=1 et chacune paie50. Si leurs annonces diffèrent, le projet est annulé et tous les paiements remboursés: Q=0, x=1000 pour chacune. Leur utilité est u(x,Q)=x+350*Q-50*Q^2-alpha*x*Q, avec alpha dans[0,1/10]. Les gains sont mesurés relativement à u(1000,0). Trouve tous les équilibres de Nash, les gains aux équilibres et le seuil de préférence entre H et L. Explique le rôle de la substitution à partir des dérivées de u. Pour une règle de sélection supplémentaire, suppose une population symétrique avec part p choisissant H et dynamique dp/dt=p*(1-p)*(gain_H-gain_L); les adversaires sont appariés indépendamment. Identifie les bassins d'attraction. Si p initial est uniforme sur[0,1], calcule la probabilité d'aboutir à H et son évolution en alpha. Vérifie alpha=0 et alpha=1/10. Sans cette dynamique et cette distribution initiale, la probabilité d'un équilibre est-elle déterminée?

A lecture suggests that if an authority knows total public-project value, cancelling whenever the reported sum is wrong makes everyone reveal their own value. Test what this conclusion actually establishes in the following complete mechanism. A and B have nonnegative monetary values vA,vB with known sum10. A project costs6. Each simultaneously reports mi in[0,10]. It is produced if and only if mA+mB=10. If produced, i pays(3/5)*mi and obtains vi-(3/5)*mi; otherwise both pay0 and obtain0. Reports need not equal values. Find the complete pure-strategy Nash equilibrium sets for values(7,3) and(5,5), separating production and cancellation. Compute truthful outcomes and exhibit a profitable deviation showing that truthfulness is not a dominant strategy. Are individual values identified by an equilibrium report pair? Can an efficient project fail even though truthful reporting is an equilibrium? Give a necessary and sufficient inequality description of the equilibria, not just counterexamples. Restrict the equilibrium classification to pure strategies.

Two households each have private wealth10 and utility xi+sqrt(y), where y>=0 is a nonrival public good. Private consumption costs1 per unit; producing the public good uses K(y)=y^2/2 units of the private good. Determine the efficient y and real surplus relative to no public good. First implement it through personalised unit prices lambda1,lambda2: household i chooses its desired y maximising10-lambdai*y+sqrt(y); a competitive supplier receives(lambda1+lambda2)*y and chooses y to maximise receipts minus K(y). Find the common-demand equilibrium, fees, household gains and supplier profit. Then compare two fully specified withdrawal contracts. In contract F, household1 has irrevocably prepaid the fee calculated in that equilibrium; household2 pays nothing; a nonprofit provider must spend exactly that fixed contribution on production and earns no profit. In contract E, household2 pays nothing, and household1 may choose any y while paying the full resource cost K(y) to a nonprofit provider. Find outputs, fees, household gains, real surpluses and efficiency ratios under F and E. Explain why observing that one person refuses to pay does not determine output without the payment contract. Derive exact answers, proving global optimality with an independent check; include supplier profit whenever computing total welfare.

Help me find a shortcut: I do not want to list every partition of twelve users. A facility gives each admitted user gross benefit12. With n>=1 users, each suffers congestion disutility n-1. Opening one facility consumes a fixed resource cost18, independent of membership. There are12 identical potential users; anyone not served receives0. A planner may open any number of facilities and choose their integer memberships, serving each user at most once. Find the complete optimal facility-size structure and total welfare, allowing some users to remain unserved. An exclusion-capable nonprofit club charges each member18/n and admits only its chosen members. Compute fees and net benefits at the optimum. As a comparison, one open-access facility is funded by an outside public budget paying18; entry is free, and individual entrants ignore their effect on existing users. Find its entry equilibrium and welfare, including the public budget cost. Finally, suppose all12 people are already in either two clubs of6 or three clubs of4, each charging equal cost shares.
