Give profit, buyer rent and real welfare for the optimal full-coverage and high-only tariffs. Compare with efficient consumption. Can a positive usage markup be optimal despite zero marginal cost?

Then ban membership fees, keeping every other assumption. Derive the best linear price globally. At alpha=3/5, compare its profit and welfare to the unrestricted optimal tariff. Does permitting a membership fee necessarily improve welfare? Check welfare both from gross utilities and from seller profit plus consumer rent. State which changes come from usage distortion and which come from exclusion.

My software gives a different p-value from plugging the pooled success rate into a binomial formula. Help me understand which randomness the exact test is using, and please specify what you mean by a two-sided p-value.

Process A is observed in four independent trials and has three successes. Process B has four independent trials and no successes. All eight trials are independent; within a process the success probability is constant. Test H0:qA=qB against qA>qB. Under H0 the common probability q is unknown and lies in(0,1). Let K be A's success count and S the total success count over both processes. The observed values are K3,S3.

Derive the conditional distribution of K given S=s under H0 and show why q disappears. For s3, calculate its probability masses, the observed upper-tail p-value, and the two-sided p-value defined as the sum of masses no larger than the observed mass. Keep this probability-ordering definition explicit.

Compare the one-sided p-value with P(Binomial(4,3/8)>=3). Explain why substituting the pooled estimate is not the same operation as conditioning. State whether the ordinary conditional upper-tail test rejects at level1/20.

Introduce an independent U uniform on[0,1] and define the randomized p-value Pstar=P(K'>K|S)+U*P(K'=K|S), where K' has the null conditional count distribution. Prove Pstar is uniform conditionally on each S and hence under the unknown common q. At the observed table, find the exact chance of rejection at level1/20. Explain what randomness does and does not change about the evidence.

Finally derive the conditional distribution under qA!=qB using their odds ratio theta. Show why larger theta favors larger K. No search over possible nuisance probabilities is needed.

Help me understand who would provide this shared service. I used the sum of everyone's investment, but the engineer says only the strongest installation determines quality. Does that change the free-rider calculation?

There are n>=2 agents. Agent i chooses investment gi>=0. Public quality is G=max(g1,...,gn), available to all agents. Utility is ui=vi*G-ki*gi^2/2, with vi>0 and ki>0. Investments and their quadratic costs are real; there are no payments or transfers. All choices are simultaneous and observable after they are made. Each agent maximizes its own utility.

Derive the full global best-response set given the largest rival investment R. Include the indifference boundary. Characterize every pure Nash equilibrium for arbitrary positive values and costs without testing investment vectors. Does a pure equilibrium always exist? Can two agents invest positively in equilibrium?

A planner chooses all investments to maximize total real welfare. Find every efficient allocation, including ties between cheapest providers. Decompose the loss of a one-provider equilibrium into quality distortion and excess provider cost.

Evaluate v=(3,6,1),k=(1,3,1). Give all pure equilibria, utilities and welfare, the efficient quality/provider choices and exact losses. Show why the higher-welfare equilibrium need not be a Pareto improvement. Check the global response of agent1 when agent2 supplies quality2. Distinguish investment in an equally strong second installation from raising the strongest installation.

Tenho três sensores, mas não observo diretamente o estado que eles tentam detectar. É possível separar a frequência do estado dos erros dos sensores usando apenas os seus resultados? Quero entender a identificação, não procurar combinações de parâmetros por tentativa.

Um estado latente T vale0 ou1, com P(T=1)=pi em(0,1). Os resultados X1,X2,X3 são binários. Condicionalmente a T, são independentes, com P(Xi=1|T=0)=ai e P(Xi=1|T=1)=bi. Assume0<=ai<bi<=1 para cada sensor; essa orientação define o significado do estado1. Nenhuma observação direta de T está disponível.

As médias observadas são mu=(3/10,7/20,2/5). As covariâncias são c12=9/100,c13=3/50,c23=9/200. O momento central de terceira ordem é m=E[(X1-mu1)*(X2-mu2)*(X3-mu3)]=9/500. São momentos exatos de população.

Derive as identidades dos momentos a partir do modelo e obtenha uma fórmula geral para pi usando m e as três covariâncias positivas. Encontre ai,bi e prove a unicidade dentro do modelo orientado. Verifique os intervalos de probabilidade e reconstrua os momentos.

Calcule P(X1=X2=X3=1) e P(T=1|X1=X2=X3=1). Faça uma verificação independente com odds e razões de verossimilhança. Explique o que acontece se a orientação ai<bi for removida, se uma covariância se anular, ou se m0 com as covariâncias ainda positivas. A compatibilidade dos momentos demonstra, por si só, independência condicional?

How can I solve the location decision before the pricing decision? I expected both shops to move toward the center to reach customers, but stronger price competition might change that reasoning.

A unit mass of consumers is uniform on[0,1]. Each must buy one unit; there is no outside option. Both firms have constant marginal cost c>=0. In stage1 they simultaneously choose locations in[0,1], which then become binding and publicly observed. In stage2 they simultaneously choose prices p_i>=c. A consumer at x minimizes p_i+t*(x-location_i)^2, with t>0. Consumer ties have measure zero when locations differ. At equal locations, lower price wins all demand and equal prices split demand equally. Profits are price markup times demand, with no location cost. Work with pure strategies at both stages.

Derive and globally verify the pure price continuation for any two distinct locations. Also resolve the co-location continuation. Reduce the location stage to payoff functions on either side of a rival's location, and derive the full global location best response, allowing a firm to move past its rival. Find every pure subgame-perfect location outcome without searching a location grid.

A planner controls locations and assignment of consumers, minimizing total transport resources. Prove its global optimum by using the centroids of assigned intervals and a completed-square identity. Compare transport cost, price, each firm's profit and total welfare between the market locations and the efficient locations when prices at the efficient locations still follow the same price game. Consumer gross benefit is a common constant V; price payments are transfers and total production cost is c. Explain how private differentiation and efficient accessibility differ.

أحاول فهم كثرة القيم الصفرية في عدد الطلبات. هل يعني الصفر أن الوحدة غير نشطة، أم يمكن أن تكون نشطة ولم يصلها أي طلب؟ وإذا حذفت الصفوف الصفرية، فما المعلومات التي أفقدها؟

افترض أن الوحدة نشطة باحتمال rho في(0,1] وغير نشطة باحتمال1-rho. الوحدة غير النشطة لها Y=0 دائما. إذا كانت نشطة فإن عدد الطلبات Y يتبع توزيع Poisson بمعلمة lambda>0. العينة الكاملة تشمل الوحدات الصفرية. متوسط المجتمع هو E[Y]=1/2، والعزم العاملي الثاني هو E[Y*(Y-1)]=1. هذه قيم دقيقة وليست تقديرات عينية.

اشتق هذين العزمين من النموذج، وحدد rho وlambda دون تجربة شبكة من المعلمات. احسب Var(Y)، واحتمال Y=0، واحتمال أن تكون الوحدة غير نشطة بعد مشاهدة Y=0. اكتب r=exp(-2) عند عرض النتائج الدقيقة التي تحتوي على دالة أسية.

إذا احتفظ الباحث فقط بالوحدات التي لها Y>0، فاشتق توزيعها الشرطي. بيّن كيف يمكن تحديد lambda من نسبة احتمالي العددين2 و1، ولماذا لا يحدد هذا التوزيع rho. احسب متوسط العينة الموجبة، واشرح لماذا لا يساوي متوسط المجتمع ولا معلمة Poisson الأصلية.

أخيرا، ابن توزيعا آخر له المتوسط والعزم العاملي الثاني نفسيهما ولكنه لا يتبع النموذج المفترض. قارن العزم العاملي الثالث. هل توافق لحظتين مع النموذج يثبت تفسير الأصفار بوصفها خليطا من نشاط وعدم نشاط؟ قدم تحققا مستقلا بدالة توليد الاحتمالات.

Help me solve this problem: I thought a minimum wage always reduces employment, but my calculation says it can increase employment here. Can you show me where the usual argument breaks and find the exact thresholds?

A single employer hires a continuum of workers. Hiring L workers produces revenue R(L)=12*L-L^2/2. Workers are ordered by their reservation wages, with inverse labor supply w_s(L)=2+L. The employer must pay all hired workers the same wage. Without regulation, obtaining L workers therefore costs (2+L)*L. There are no other costs or outside profits.

A binding legal wage floor m>=2 permits the employer to hire any L<=m-2 at wage m. To hire more than m-2 workers it must pay 2+L. If labor is rationed, assume the lowest-reservation-wage workers are selected; their total opportunity cost is the integral of 2+x from x=0 to x=L. Workers not hired receive no surplus.

Find the unregulated employment and wage. Derive the employer's globally optimal employment and actual wage for every floor m>=2, including shutdown. Identify which floors improve employment and total surplus relative to no regulation, and which floor maximizes total surplus. Compute employment, employer profit, worker surplus and total surplus at m=6 and m=9. Explain why the payment bill differs from the social opportunity cost, and how arbitrary rationing would affect the welfare calculation. Use an independent check rather than a numerical grid.

Ich weiß nicht, wie ich diese Insolvenzfrage ohne eine Normalverteilungsannahme lösen soll. Kannst du mir einen kurzen mathematischen Weg zeigen und erklären, ob die Schranke wirklich erreichbar ist?

Der zufällige operative Gewinn X eines Unternehmens hat E[X]=6 und Var(X)=9. Weitere Verteilungsannahmen gibt es nicht; negative Gewinne sind erlaubt. Ein Unternehmen gilt bei X<=0 als insolvent. Bestimme die größte mögliche Insolvenzwahrscheinlichkeit über alle Verteilungen mit diesen beiden Momenten. Beweise die Schranke und konstruiere eine Verteilung, die sie erreicht.

Was ändert sich, wenn Insolvenz strikt als X<0 definiert wird? Unterscheide Maximum und Supremum. Zeige eine Familie von Verteilungen mit den vorgegebenen Momenten, deren strikte Verlustwahrscheinlichkeit gegen das Supremum geht.

Eine sichere Reserve k>=0 wird zum Gewinn addiert. Finde die kleinste Reserve, die P(X+k<=0)<=1/20 für jede zulässige Verteilung garantiert. Vergleiche die einseitige Schranke mit der gewöhnlichen zweiseitigen Chebyshev-Schranke bei k=0.

Schließlich werden n unabhängige Gewinne mit derselben Verteilung gemittelt. Wie viele Unternehmen genügen nach dieser einseitigen Schranke, um P(Mittelwert<=0)<=1/100 zu garantieren? Ist die hergeleitete Schranke unter dieser zusätzlichen Unabhängigkeitsstruktur automatisch scharf? Erkläre auch, warum die Rechnung bei perfekt gemeinsamen Gewinnen nicht gilt.

Je ne comprends pas et je ne sais pas comment résoudre ce problème de financement collectif. Si les promesses sont remboursées quand le projet échoue, est-ce que cela supprime vraiment le problème du passager clandestin ? Aide-moi à trouver tous les équilibres sans essayer des centaines de montants.

Trois personnes bénéficient chacune de 6 si un projet public est réalisé. Son coût fixe est 9. Elles choisissent simultanément des promesses g_i dans [0,9]. Le projet est réalisé si S=g_1+g_2+g_3>=9. Dans ce cas chaque personne paie sa promesse et reçoit l'utilité 6-g_i. Si S<9, le projet échoue, toutes les promesses sont remboursées et chaque utilité vaut 0. Une promesse excédant le coût n'est pas remboursée si le projet réussit. Les préférences sont quasi linéaires et l'utilité hors projet est 0.

Caractérise exactement tous les équilibres de Nash purs qui réussissent et ceux qui échouent. Les joueurs peuvent être indifférents : ne remplace pas les inégalités faibles par des inégalités strictes. Trouve le plus grand total de promesses possible à un équilibre d'échec, ainsi qu'un équilibre symétrique de réussite. Compare les utilités et la stabilité face à une coalition de trois personnes.

Refais ensuite la caractérisation si les promesses sont payées même quand le projet échoue. Le remboursement garantit-il la réalisation du projet ? Explique comment la somme des deux promesses adverses permet de réduire ce jeu continu à un calcul de meilleure réponse.

Can you check my approach? I tried to make every action indifferent for every cost, but some probabilities become negative. How can I find the right equilibrium without enumerating all possible supports?

A row player maximizes a zero-sum payoff and a column player minimizes it. Each chooses one of three sectors. If they choose the same sector, the row player receives 2 in sector 1, 3 in sector 2, or 6 in sector 3; different sectors give a gross payoff of 0. Choosing row action 1 additionally subtracts k>=0 from the row payoff regardless of the column action. The column payoff is the negative of the resulting row payoff, including this cost term. This is a strategic zero-sum model, not a claim about total social welfare.

Thus the row payoff matrix has rows (2-k,-k,-k), (0,3,0), and (0,0,6). Write p for the row probability vector and q for the column probability vector.

Derive the game value and all Nash equilibrium strategies for every k>=0. Include the boundary where full-support mixing ceases, and prove completeness using security inequalities. Give exact strategies and net and gross expected payoff at k=1. Explain which player's probabilities solve which indifference equations. Finally interpret the slope of the value with respect to k away from the boundary, and verify it through direct equilibrium payoffs.

How can I solve this without optimizing separately for lots of possible signals? I keep confusing the policy for the average damage with the average of the optimal policies.

A decision maker chooses activity q>=0, obtaining private benefit B(q)=12*q-q^2/2. External damage is D(q,theta)=theta*q^2/2. The damage coefficient theta is 1 or 5, each with prior probability 1/2. Welfare is B-D. The regulator is risk neutral and must choose q before observing theta, unless information is purchased. There are no other resource costs.

A binary signal reports either low or high. Its accuracy is p in [1/2,1]: P(low|theta=1)=P(high|theta=5)=p. Conditional on the signal the regulator chooses q, but still cannot observe theta directly. The signal is informative only about damage. A per-unit tax t can implement q because the private decision maker maximizes B(q)-t*q. Tax receipts are rebated through transfers independent of q, with no excess funding cost.

Find the no-information and perfect-information policies and expected welfare. Derive the posterior-optimal policy and tax after each signal, and expected welfare as a function of p. At p=3/4, compute the policies, taxes and value of information. Compare the correct policies to the posterior averages of the statewise optimal quantities, and quantify the welfare loss from using those averages.

Finally, purchasing accuracy p has real resource cost C(p)=kappa*(p-1/2)^2, with kappa>=0. Characterize every optimal accuracy, including the tie case. Use curvature to rule out intermediate optima and verify welfare through a completed-square identity.

Peux-tu vérifier ma correction ? J'ai utilisé la perte totale de surplus comme amende, mais l'entreprise semble encore vouloir exclure sa rivale. Je voudrais comprendre le calcul économique, pas seulement remplacer des nombres dans une formule.

Deux entreprises choisissent simultanément q0,q1>=0. Les demandes inverses sont p0=24-4*q0-2*q1 et p1=24-4*q1-2*q0. Les coûts sont C0=4*q0 et C1=q1^2. L'utilité brute des consommateurs est U=24*(q0+q1)-2*(q0^2+q1^2)-2*q0*q1. Le surplus des consommateurs vaut U-p0*q0-p1*q1, et le surplus total vaut U-C0-C1.

L'entreprise0 peut exclure illégalement le produit1 et devenir le monopole du seul produit0; les primitives restantes sont inchangées. Calcule les équilibres de Cournot et de monopole, puis les variations monopole moins Cournot du surplus des consommateurs, du profit total et du surplus total. Trouve aussi l'allocation socialement efficace avec les deux produits et la perte de Cournot relativement à cette allocation.

Pour la sanction, note Delta le gain privé de l'entreprise0 lié à l'exclusion. La probabilité de détection est 1/2 et, conditionnellement à la détection, celle de condamnation est 1/2. Si elle est condamnée, elle rend exactement Delta et paie une amende additionnelle f>=0. Sinon elle conserve Delta. Elle est neutre au risque. Trouve l'amende minimale de dissuasion faible et explique le cas d'égalité. Une amende égale à la perte totale de surplus suffit-elle ? Que devient le minimum si la condamnation impose seulement l'amende, sans restitution de Delta ?

Distingue le gain privé, la variation des profits de toutes les entreprises et le dommage collectif. Vérifie le surplus par deux routes et démontre que l'optimum social trouvé est global.

Help me understand why moving first can benefit both firms here. If both profits increase, does that mean price commitment is good for the economy?

Two differentiated products have demands q1=2-p1+p2/2 and q2=2-p2+p1/2. Firm1 has constant marginal cost1 and firm2 has constant marginal cost1/2. Each maximizes (p_i-c_i)*q_i. For a globally specified game, restrict prices to p1 in [1,9/4] and p2 in [1/2,2]; both demands are nonnegative throughout this rectangle. There are no fixed costs. These bounds retain the source model's interior solutions.

Compare simultaneous price choice to sequential choice where firm1 commits to its price and firm2 observes it before choosing. Find the unique equilibrium of each game and both firms' profit changes. Prove that the strategies are global best responses on the stated domains. Show how a completed square gives the leader's commitment gain without re-expanding two profit formulas.

Consumers have quasilinear preferences consistent with the given demand system, and tax-free resource welfare is utility minus production costs. Recover inverse demands and utility normalized by U(0,0)=0. Compute consumer surplus and total welfare under both games. Determine the efficient allocation and compare the two equilibrium welfare losses with an independent quadratic check. Explain why profit gains alone do not settle the welfare comparison.

Can you explain this apparent contradiction? A randomized job-training programme triples the employment odds in every group, but the overall odds ratio is smaller than three. Does that prove the randomization failed, or that controlling for the group created bias?

Let T be randomized programme assignment, independent of a pre-treatment group Z. Each group has population share1/2. In group Z=0 the employment probabilities are P(Y=1|T=0,Z=0)=1/10 and P(Y=1|T=1,Z=0)=1/4. In group Z=1 they are P(Y=1|T=0,Z=1)=1/2 and P(Y=1|T=1,Z=1)=3/4. Assume consistency and random assignment, so these conditional risks have a causal interpretation for the respective groups. All probabilities are exact population values.

Compute each group's odds ratio, the marginal risks and marginal odds ratio, and the population average treatment effect on the probability scale. Compare the group risk differences and risk ratios. Explain why the difference between conditional and marginal odds ratios need not be confounding.

Generalize: suppose baseline employment risk is a random variable B in (0,1), and treatment multiplies the conditional odds by a common factor rho>1. Derive the treated-risk map f_rho(B). Prove that with equal group composition across assignments, a nonconstant B gives a marginal odds ratio strictly between1 and rho. Find the exact Jensen gap for two baseline values x,y with weights w,1-w, and verify it in the numerical example.

Finally, change the target population so that group0 has share3/4 while the groupwise risks remain unchanged. Standardize both assignments to this same new population. Recompute the marginal odds ratio and average treatment effect. Does a common conditional odds ratio define a population-invariant marginal effect?

Non capisco perché uno stimatore possa essere corretto quando uno dei due modelli è sbagliato. Puoi aiutarmi a dimostrarlo, invece di citare soltanto la doppia robustezza?

In un'indagine economica X assume0 oppure1, ciascuno con probabilità1/2. Il risultato Y ha media condizionata m(0)=2, m(1)=6 e varianza condizionata1 in entrambi i gruppi. Il risultato viene osservato soltanto se R=1. Le probabilità di risposta sono e(0)=1/4, e(1)=3/4. Assumi R indipendente da Y condizionatamente a X, e osserva X anche per chi non risponde. L'obiettivo è mu=E[Y].

Per funzioni fissate g(X)>0 e h(X), considera lo score osservabile psi=h(X)+R*(Y-h(X))/g(X). Quando R=0, il termine con Y è definito come0 senza osservare Y. Le funzioni g e h non sono adattate usando la stessa osservazione sulla quale si valuta lo score.

Deriva la media dello score e un'identità esatta per il suo bias. Dimostra la doppia robustezza, ma verifica anche se l'assenza di bias implica necessariamente che almeno uno dei due modelli sia corretto. Calcola il bias per g=(1/2,1/2) con h=(1,5), poi con h=(1,4). Nel primo caso confronta lo score con la sola ponderazione R*Y/g(X) e con la sola previsione h(X).

Con g=e, deriva la varianza per qualsiasi h fissata e prova quale h la minimizza. Calcola le varianze dello score con h=m, della sola ponderazione R*Y/e(X), e dello score con h=(1,5). Mostra anche perché perturbare simultaneamente entrambi i modelli attorno ai valori corretti produce bias di secondo ordine. Spiega i limiti dovuti alla positività e all'uso della stessa osservazione per adattare i modelli.

Can you help me check this derivation? The correction writes one monopoly condition as 4-6*q2+4*q1=0, but then claims q1=q2=2/5. I want a structural check of the sign, not just the final numbers.

Consumers have quasilinear utility in a numeraire plus V(q1,q2)=5*(q1+q2)-(3*q1^2+4*q1*q2+3*q2^2)/2. Quantities are nonnegative, marginal costs of both goods are1, and numeraire wealth is sufficient for the allocations considered. A single owner can choose any nonnegative quantity vector and charge the associated inverse-demand prices. Its objective is total profit, not social welfare.

First recover inverse and direct demands. Derive the correct monopoly conditions and prove the global optimum using total quantity u=q1+q2 and imbalance d=q1-q2. Explain why the displayed plus sign cannot be correct.

Then consider separate firms choosing prices simultaneously in [1,7/3] each. These explicitly imposed bounds make the direct demand formulas nonnegative at every allowed profile; they do not constrain the single owner's quantity choice. Derive the unique price equilibrium and verify global best responses on these intervals.

Compute prices, quantities, consumer surplus, total profit and total welfare under each ownership regime. Find the globally efficient allocation and the two efficiency ratios. Check the welfare losses using a completed square, and explain why joint ownership internalizes a demand cross effect that separate firms omit.

How can adding experts make an economic-policy decision worse if every expert is right three quarters of the time? Help me identify the dependence assumption and find the optimal way to combine their reports.

The correct policy state S is0 or1 with equal prior probability. All experts report their binary signals honestly; there is no strategic voting or reporting choice. A panel shares an unobserved accuracy regime Theta, independent of S. With probability2/3, Theta=1; with probability1/3, Theta=1/4. Conditional on S and Theta, experts' signals are independent and each equals S with probability Theta. Neither the decision maker nor the experts observe Theta.

Let C_i indicate that expert i is correct. Find each expert's marginal accuracy, the covariance and correlation of two correctness indicators, and the variance of their average. Compute the accuracy of simple majority for panels of3 and5, and its limit along odd panel sizes. Compare the answers to the counterfactual of genuinely independent correctness indicators with the same marginal accuracy.

For an odd panel size n, let K be the number of reports equal to1. Derive the Bayes-optimal policy decision from the likelihood ratio for every possible K, including unanimous reports. Compute its accuracy for n=3 and n=5 and its large-panel limit. For n=3, give the posterior probability of S=1 at K=1 and at K=3. Explain why this is an aggregation problem rather than a claim that truthful voting is a strategic equilibrium.

Kannst du mir erklären, warum vollständige Versicherung nicht automatisch eine Aufteilung zu gleichen Teilen bedeutet? Ich dachte, bei gleichem Gesamteinkommen in beiden Zuständen müssten beide Personen am Ende jeweils5 erhalten.

Es gibt zwei Zustände s=0,1 mit gemeinsamen Wahrscheinlichkeiten1/4 und3/4. Person A besitzt zustandsabhängige Ausstattung (8,2), Person B besitzt (2,8). In jedem Zustand ist der einzige Konsumgutbestand somit10. Beide Personen haben erwarteten Nutzen U_i=(1/4)*log(c_i0)+(3/4)*log(c_i1), mit strikt positivem Konsum. Es gibt keine Produktion und keine Transaktionskosten.

In vollständigen Märkten handeln sie vor Eintritt des Zustands zustandsabhängige Ansprüche. Preise pi0,pi1 sind positiv und auf pi0+pi1=1 normiert. Jede Person maximiert ihren erwarteten Nutzen unter pi0*c_i0+pi1*c_i1<=pi0*e_i0+pi1*e_i1. In jedem Zustand müssen die Konsumgüterbestände aufgehen.

Bestimme die gesamte Pareto-effiziente Allokationsmenge und begründe sie global. Finde das Wettbewerbsgleichgewicht, die normierten Zustandspreise und die Nettoübertragungen in beiden Zuständen. Berechne die Sicherheitsäquivalente ohne Handel und nach dem Gleichgewichtshandel.

Prüfe, ob die feste Gleichaufteilung (5,5) für jede Person gegenüber Autarkie freiwillig akzeptiert wird. Finde das vollständige Intervall konstanter Versicherungsallokationen (x,10-x), die beide Personen gegenüber Autarkie schwach bevorzugen. Welche Vermögensübertragung zu den Gleichgewichtspreisen wäre nötig, um gleiche Versicherungsansprüche zu finanzieren?

Zeige zuletzt, wie A ihre Gleichgewichtsübertragungen durch eine risikolose Forderung mit Auszahlung1 in jedem Zustand und eine Forderung mit Auszahlung1 nur in Zustand0 umsetzen kann. Leerverkäufe und negative Bestände dieser Verträge sind erlaubt. Prüfe Kosten und Güterbilanz unabhängig.

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi une certification volontaire peut réduire le surplus total. Si chaque vendeur choisit ce qui lui rapporte le plus, où est la perte ? Aide-moi à trouver l'équilibre par une équation plutôt qu'en essayant des seuils.

Une masse1 de vendeurs possède chacun un objet de qualité x, distribuée uniformément sur[0,1]. Le vendeur connaît sa qualité et sa valeur de conservation est0. Chaque objet est vendu dans tous les cas. Les acheteurs sont neutres au risque et valorisent l'objet à x. La concurrence entre acheteurs impose un prix égal à la qualité moyenne conditionnelle aux informations publiques.

Avant la vente, un vendeur peut obtenir une preuve parfaitement vérifiable de sa qualité au coût réel h>=0. S'il certifie, son prix est x et son revenu net x-h. Sans certification, tous les vendeurs reçoivent le prix commun p_s égal à E[x|silence] quand le silence a une masse positive. La preuve ne peut pas être falsifiée. Les vendeurs sont neutres au risque. Au point d'indifférence, l'une ou l'autre décision est permise.

Caractérise tous les équilibres en seuil pour tous les coûts h>=0, y compris h=0 et h=1/2. Justifie pourquoi la structure de seuil découle de l'incitation, et non d'une hypothèse arbitraire. À coût nul, précise la croyance nécessaire au silence hors trajectoire. Calcule la masse qui certifie, le paiement brut moyen aux vendeurs, le coût réel total et le surplus total.

Fais les calculs exacts pour h=1/10. Trouve le coût qui maximise la perte de surplus liée à la certification. Compare avec une interdiction de certifier, sous laquelle tous les objets restent vendus au prix moyen. Explique pourquoi cette conclusion dépend de l'absence de gain d'allocation dans le modèle et ne prouve pas que l'information est toujours inutile.

How can I solve a Stackelberg market with several leaders without writing a huge system? Is moving early still an advantage when the early firms compete against each other?

Inverse demand is p=1-Q and all firms have zero production costs. Quantities are nonnegative. There are n>=1 early firms and r>=1 late firms, both integer counts. Early firms choose binding quantities simultaneously. Every late firm observes the entire early quantity vector; late firms then choose quantities simultaneously. All quantities are sold at the final market price. The affine price has no floor, so excessive off-path output can give a negative price. There are no entry decisions or fixed costs.

Find the unique pure subgame-perfect quantity outcome for arbitrary n,r and prove the follower continuation after every early quantity vector. Show why an early firm's global best response can be found from a one-variable quadratic despite the possible follower shutdown.

Compare each early and late firm's profit with that in simultaneous Cournot among all n+r firms. Give the exact condition under which an early firm gains, ties or loses from early commitment. Compare prices, total output and resource welfare, with gross consumer benefit Q-Q^2/2.

For n=2,r=1, give quantities, profits, consumer surplus and total welfare under both timings. Check how all firms can lose profit while welfare rises.

Finally, replace the n competing early firms by one joint owner who can distribute its early output freely across them. Find the total committed output, follower quantities, price and aggregate early profit. Explain how joint ownership changes output and welfare, and characterize any nonuniqueness in the division of early output.

Can you help me solve this dominant-firm model analytically? The fringe supply contains a square root, and I do not want to search over prices. I also want to know whether more fringe firms must drive the dominant firm's output to zero.

Market demand is D(p)=max(0,v-p), with v>0. A dominant firm has zero marginal cost and unlimited capacity. It commits to a price p>=0 and serves residual demand. The competitive fringe has exogenous mass n>=0 of identical price takers. Each unit of fringe mass chooses output y>=0 to maximize p*y-y^3/3. Thus total fringe cost is n*y^3/3. The mass n is a continuous scale parameter, not an endogenous entry choice; when n=0 there is no fringe.

Only prices satisfying D(p)>=n*y(p) are feasible for the dominant firm. It earns p*[D(p)-n*y(p)]. All output is sold, there are no fixed costs, and gross consumer benefit is v*Q-Q^2/2.

Derive fringe supply and the dominant firm's unique global optimum for every n>=0. Use t=sqrt(p) to find an exact positive root and a rationalized representation of it. Find the price, dominant output, fringe output and both profit totals. Prove feasibility and compare with the monopoly limit n=0.

By implicit differentiation, determine how t, dominant output, total fringe output and welfare change with n. Derive the efficient resource benchmark and decompose the welfare loss into an output distortion and a production-allocation cost. Compute the limits as n becomes arbitrarily large, including the dominant firm's output and market share.

For v=7/2,n=1, give price, both outputs, consumer surplus, both profit totals and welfare. Check the surplus ledger independently from gross benefit minus real cost.

Mi aiuti a capire questo esercizio? Non vedo come collegare l'equilibrio dei prezzi alla perdita di benessere. Un consumatore di ogni posizione x in [0,1], con densità uniforme, acquista esattamente un'unità. Due imprese sono localizzate in 0 e 1. Il costo di trasporto è t volte il quadrato della distanza, con t>0. I costi marginali delle imprese sono rispettivamente 0 e alpha, con 0<=alpha<=t. Ogni impresa sceglie un prezzo in [0,2*t]. Il valore lordo comune v>=3*t garantisce la copertura del mercato; in caso di indifferenza con l'opzione esterna il consumatore acquista. Un consumatore indifferente tra imprese può essere assegnato arbitrariamente, essendo un insieme di misura zero. Ricava l'equilibrio di Nash puro e giustifica che nessuna deviazione globale è profittevole. Trova la frontiera efficiente di assegnazione, la perdita di benessere e perché una quota maggiore dell'impresa efficiente non implica necessariamente meno trasporto. Controlla tutto con t=3, alpha=3/2, mantenendo v simbolico. Non cercare l'equilibrio enumerando prezzi.

Aide-moi à vérifier cette idée: une punition très courte pourrait soutenir un cartel avec moins de patience qu'un retour définitif à Cournot. Mais pourquoi les entreprises accepteraient-elles de punir?

Deux entreprises à coût nul choisissent simultanément q_i dans[0,1] chaque période, avec prix p=1-q1-q2 et profit p*q_i. Un prix négatif est permis par cette formule pour les déviations hors trajectoire. Les quantités sont publiquement observées et le facteur d'actualisation commun est delta dans[0,1). Le jeu est infini. L'état initial C prescrit q1=q2=1/4. Toute déviation conduit à l'état P à la période suivante. Dans P, chacune produit x, fixé une fois pour toutes dans[1/3,1/2]. Si toutes deux respectent P, on revient à C dès la période suivante; toute déviation dans P maintient P à la période suivante. Aucun transfert n'est possible. Les entreprises peuvent respecter une prescription même si elles sont indifférentes.

Trouve les contraintes exactes dans les deux états et le x qui minimise le facteur d'actualisation nécessaire pour que ce profil soit un équilibre parfait en sous-jeux. Compare au retour définitif à Cournot et vérifie les valeurs de continuation au seuil optimal. Calcule aussi le bien-être instantané dans C, P optimal et Cournot, avec bénéfice brut Q-Q^2/2. Ne conclus pas qu'un seuil trouvé est optimal parmi toutes les stratégies possibles: optimise seulement la famille définie ici.

Help me find the missing assumption in this backward-induction argument: because the game ends at a known date, cooperation must disappear in every period.

Two players play a symmetric stage game with actions C,D,R and payoff pairs: CC:(3,3), CD:(0,5), DC:(5,0), DD:(1,1), RR:(4,4). Every other pair has payoffs(0,0). Actions are publicly observed. There are T>=2 periods, known in advance, with discount factor delta in[0,1], and no outside transfers. A strategy prescribes CC in every period before T while all previous outcomes have been CC. At T it prescribes RR if the entire earlier history consists of CC. Following any other earlier outcome, it prescribes DD for every remaining period, including T. Indifferent players may follow the prescription.

Find all pure stage-game Nash equilibria. For T=2, derive the effective first-period payoff matrix under the prescribed terminal strategies and characterize every pure first-period equilibrium. Determine exactly when the stated cooperation strategy is subgame-perfect for every finite T>=2, using a formula in the number of remaining cooperative periods instead of enumerating histories. Check payoffs and deviations at T=3,delta=3/4. Explain the precise reason finite-horizon unraveling does or does not apply, without claiming that arbitrary finite repeated games permit cooperation.

How can a strictly concave harvesting game have many equilibria? Help me solve the model and check whether using a single resource shadow price silently removes solutions.

Two users harvest h1,h2>=0 from a common stock of size K>0. The physical constraint is h1+h2<=K. Taking the other's harvest as fixed, user i may deviate only within[0,K-hj]. This shared-constraint game is a generalized Nash game: each equilibrium must be feasible and each chosen harvest must maximize that user's payoff over its own feasible interval. The payoff is hi*(v-h1-h2), where v>0. This is a direct real benefit from harvesting, with no outside buyers or extra consumer surplus. Negative per-unit benefit is permitted in the formula, but users can choose zero. Social welfare is the sum of these two payoffs.

Characterize the complete generalized Nash set for all K,v without enumerating candidate allocations. Compare it with the common-multiplier selection: user-specific KKT resource multipliers must be identical. Find an exact potential and use its global maximum to characterize that selection, while explaining why this does not characterize every generalized Nash equilibrium. Derive the efficient total harvest and the equilibrium welfare loss in all stock regimes. Check v=2 with K=1,6/5,2, including allocation intervals, selected allocations and welfare. Preserve a set-valued answer where necessary.

Help me solve this tax-competition problem rigorously. I know that taxes transfer money, but here they finance something useful. Does coordination still merely increase receipts?

Two jurisdictions each own one unit of a fixed total capital stock2, and residents may invest it freely across jurisdictions. Production in each is F(k)=4*k-k^2/2. Competitive capital earns a common after-tax rental r0. Each government simultaneously chooses a unit capital tax ti in(0,1], then capital is competitively allocated with ki>=0,k1+k2=2 and F'(ki)-ti=r0 in active locations. Local residents own the local immobile production factor, receiving residual firm income F(ki)-F'(ki)*ki, as well as rental r0 on their one owned capital unit. They consume all private income. Tax receipts Gi=ti*ki finance a local public good with real unit production cost1; they are spent, not rebated. Jurisdiction i's objective is private income plus(1/2)*log(Gi). The logarithm is natural. For reporting the final welfare gain, define r=log(5/4); r is a constant, distinct from the capital rental r0. No other resource costs or externalities apply.

Derive capital allocation and each government's objective for every permitted tax pair. Prove the unique pure tax equilibrium, including global own-tax optimality and uniqueness rather than simply imposing symmetry. Then maximize the sum of the two objectives over the same tax domain. Use mean-and-difference coordinates to prove the coordinated optimum is global. Compare production, private consumption, public-good expenditures and total welfare. Give the exact gain using r and prove its sign analytically. Explain why counting both spending and tax receipts as benefits would be wrong.

Ich habe die Erfolgsquoten einfach sortiert, damit sie mit der Förderintensität steigen. Ist das eine zulässige Schätzung? Bitte zeige mir einen besseren mathematischen Weg, ohne mögliche Wahrscheinlichkeitsvektoren durchzuprobieren.

Vier voneinander unabhängige Gruppen haben feste Stichprobengrößen n=(4,6,5,5) und beobachtete Erfolgszahlen s=(3,1,4,3). In Gruppe i gilt Si~Binomial(ni,pi). Die Gruppen stehen in einer festen Reihenfolge steigender Förderintensität; Beobachtungen dürfen nicht zwischen Gruppen verschoben werden. Gesucht ist die Maximum-Likelihood-Schätzung unter0<=p1<=p2<=p3<=p4<=1. Die Ordnung ist eine angenommene Formrestriktion, keine aus den Daten bewiesene kausale Wirkung.

Leite die Schätzung her und beweise ihre globale Eindeutigkeit mit Konkavität und passenden Multiplikatoren. Erkläre, warum das Zusammenlegen benachbarter Gruppen gewichtete Quoten braucht. Berechne das exakte Likelihood-Verhältnis Lambda=L(geordnetes Maximum)/L(unbeschränktes Maximum), wobei die Binomialkoeffizienten kürzbar sind. Gib die Teststatistik als-2*log(Lambda) an und erkläre, warum du dafür nicht ohne weitere Herleitung eine gewöhnliche Chi-Quadrat-Kalibrierung behaupten darfst. Prüfe das Ergebnis unabhängig mit den zusammengelegten Binomial-Likelihoods und den Vorzeichen der Randableitungen.

Je ne comprends pas cette affirmation: toute allocation efficace serait obtenue en maximisant une somme pondérée des utilités. Peux-tu vérifier ce qui manque, puis me montrer ce que change une loterie?

Deux personnes se partagent une unité de ressource: x1,x2>=0,x1+x2<=1. Les utilités déterministes sont u1=x1^2,u2=x2^2. Si une loterie est autorisée, chaque réalisation doit respecter la même contrainte physique et chaque personne évalue la loterie par E[x_i^2]; ce sont les utilités espérées déclarées du modèle. Aucune autre attitude face au risque ne doit être supposée.

Caractérise la frontière de Pareto déterministe et les maximisateurs de lambda*u1+(1-lambda)*u2 pour tout lambda dans[0,1]. Trouve aussi l'allocation déterministe maximisant le produit de Nash u1*u2 avec point de désaccord(0,0). Décris ensuite exactement tout l'ensemble d'utilités espérées réalisables par loteries, sa frontière de Pareto et son maximum du produit de Nash. Montre explicitement comment une loterie peut dominer strictement le partage déterministe égal sans dépasser la ressource dans aucune réalisation. Compare les conditions de participation pour des utilités de réservation(a,b)>=0, puis décide pour(a,b)=(1/3,1/3). Distingue efficacité déterministe, efficacité avec randomisation et égalité des utilités réalisées.

Help me understand how reputation could make an incumbent fight today even though fighting is unprofitable in the last market. Please derive the beliefs and incentives together, rather than assuming a threat works.

There are two successive markets and a different potential entrant in each. The first entrant has already entered, so its entry decision is not part of the game being solved. Nature selects the incumbent's type: a committed type with probability alpha in(0,1/2), which mechanically fights every entry, or a strategic type otherwise. The incumbent knows its type. Against entry, the strategic type chooses fight F with current profit-1 or accommodate A with current profit2. Without entry it earns6. It discounts second-market profit by delta in[0,1]. The committed type's prescribed behavior is a primitive, not a profit-maximization claim.

The second entrant observes the first-market action but not the type. It chooses In or Out. Out pays it0. In pays it-1 if fought and1 if accommodated. After In in the second market, the strategic incumbent chooses F or A with the same current profits and no later market. Indifferent strategic players and the second entrant may mix. Entrant payoffs have no other costs.

Characterize every perfect Bayesian equilibrium continuation from the already-entered first market, for every delta, including the equality case. Let f be the strategic type's probability of fighting in market1 and g the second entrant's entry probability after F. Compute posteriors, f and g, and the first entrant's expected payoff as a counterfactual assessment of its already-committed entry. Check alpha=1/4,delta=1 exactly, including the strategic incumbent's continuation values and the probability of first-market fighting. Do not claim you have solved the larger game with an endogenous first entry decision.

このリスク計算を手伝ってください。損失の90%分位点がゼロなら、安全な配分と言ってよいのでしょうか。数多くの配分を試すのでなく、式から最適解を求めたいです。

仮想的な二つの政策A,Bの損失は、同じ三つの状態でそれぞれA=(10,0,0),B=(0,4,1)です。状態確率は(1/20,3/20,4/5)。配分x in[0,1]の損失はL(x)=x*A+(1-x)*Bとし、これは確率的にどちらかの政策を選ぶことではなく、各状態で損失を線形に組み合わせることです。VaR90=inf{z:P(L<=z)>=9/10}。ES90は上側10%の平均損失と定義し、分位点に確率質量があれば必要な部分だけを採用します。同値な式ES90=min_z[z+10*E[(L-z)_+]]も使えます。

すべてのxについてVaR90,ES90,平均損失を導き、各基準を最小にする配分を求めてください。ES最適解の大域性を証明し、x=1との違いを説明してください。分位点以上の損失の条件付き平均E[L|L>=VaR90]をESと同一視してよいかも検証してください。別の計算経路として、確率密度の重みxiを0<=xi<=10かつsum_s p_s*xi_s=1の範囲で選び、sum_s p_s*xi_s*L_sの最大値を確認してください。

Peux-tu m'aider à trouver un raccourci général plutôt que recalculer chaque monopole? Je soupçonne que la perte relative de surplus reste la même avec plusieurs produits, même quand certains ne sont pas vendus.

Considère U(q)=a'*q-(1/2)*q'*A*q, où A est symétrique définie positive. Le coût réel est c'*q, sans coût fixe. Les prix inverses sont a-A*q et le propriétaire unique maximise Pi(q)=(a-c)'*q-q'*A*q. Le planificateur maximise W(q)=(a-c)'*q-(1/2)*q'*A*q. L'ensemble réalisable C est un cône fermé convexe dans les quantités non négatives: q in C implique k*q in C pour tout k>=0. Les deux problèmes ont le même C. Suppose que le surplus optimal est strictement positif. Prouve une relation exacte entre les quantités privées et efficaces et calcule W(monopole)/W(optimum), sans supposer une solution intérieure ni inverser A.

Applique ensuite le résultat à U=4*(q1+q2)-(q1^2+q1*q2+q2^2)/2, avec q1,q2>=0 et coûts unitaires c1=1,c2=t, où t>=0. Trouve tous les régimes de quantités du monopole et du planificateur, et justifie le produit arrêté par sa dérivée au bord. Pour t=1 et3, donne quantités, profit total, surplus des consommateurs et surplus total, plus le benchmark efficace. Enfin, pour t=1 ajoute la capacité q1+q2<=1 aux deux problèmes. Recalcule leurs allocations et le rapport de surplus, puis explique précisément pourquoi le théorème précédent ne s'applique plus.

Je ne comprends pas pourquoi le simple fait d'observer une quantité change la réponse, alors qu'à l'équilibre le follower finit par choisir la même quantité dans les deux cas. Peux-tu résoudre le jeu et montrer où ma dérivée se trompe?

Deux entreprises à coût nul vendent un bien homogène avec prix p=1-q1-q2. L'entreprise1 choisit irréversiblement q1 dans[0,1]. Ensuite, indépendamment de cette quantité, la nature révèle parfaitement q1 à l'entreprise2 avec probabilité alpha dans[0,1]. Avec probabilité1-alpha, elle lui indique seulement que la quantité a été choisie, sans la révéler. Le statut observé/non observé est connu de l'entreprise2. Elle choisit alors q2>=0, et les ventes ont lieu. Le profit de chacune est p*qi; la formule autorise des prix négatifs hors trajectoire. Les joueurs connaissent alpha. Le choix de q1 n'est jamais révisé. Un événement de probabilité nulle peut être supprimé du jeu.

Détermine tous les résultats d'équilibre bayésien parfait, en autorisant au départ les stratégies mixtes. Donne la réponse après observation, la croyance et la réponse sans observation, puis certifie l'optimum global du leader. Compare les quantités, les profits individuels, le profit agrégé et le surplus total lorsque alpha augmente. Utilise W=Q-Q^2/2, sans autres coûts. Vérifie alpha=1/2 et les limites0 et1. Mon calcul remplace avant dérivation toute réponse du follower par(1-q1)/2, même dans la branche non observée: explique exactement pourquoi cela ne décrit pas une déviation unilatérale.

请帮我检查这个判断：两个概率预测都校准，取平均后也应该校准，而且平均一定是最佳预测。能不能用精确的数学证明或反例说明，而不是试很多聚合规则？

一个经济事件Y取0或1，先验P(Y=1)=1/2。两个信号S1,S2也取0或1，给定Y后相互独立，且P(Si=Y|Y)=3/4。每个预测器只看自己的信号，给出Fi=P(Y=1|Si)。我使用平均M=(F1+F2)/2。校准指P(Y=1|预测值)=该预测值，损失为Brier平方损失(预测值-Y)^2。这是完整的假设分布，不是观察到的样本频率。

证明每个Fi校准。用正信号数K=S1+S2推导全部联合后验R=P(Y=1|S1,S2)、M以及K的概率。判断M是否校准，给出保持平均值信息的精确再校准公式。求单个Fi、M和R的期望Brier损失，用条件平方分解证明R在所有基于两信号的预测中全局最优。再用无条件二阶矩独立核验M的损失，并解释为什么均值正确和损失改善仍不足以证明校准。说明给定Y的独立性在你的贝叶斯聚合中起什么作用。

How should I solve bargaining when the proposer is randomly selected rather than alternating? Does being selected more often matter more than patience? Please find a structural formula instead of unfolding infinitely many offers.

Two players divide a unit resource, with nonnegative shares summing to1. At the start of each period, independently of all history, player1 is selected to propose with probability alpha in(0,1), and player2 otherwise. The selected player offers a division, and the other observes it and accepts or rejects. Acceptance ends the game with the offered shares. Rejection gives no current payoff and starts a fresh period. Player1 discounts future shares by delta in[0,1), player2 by s in[0,1). Infinite disagreement pays0. Responders accept at indifference. Utilities are linear in their own shares.

Characterize stationary subgame-perfect equilibrium values measured before proposer selection, and the offers conditional on each proposer. Stationary means strategies and continuation values depend on the current proposer and offer, not on earlier history. Prove that every stationary equilibrium agrees immediately, then show global optimality of the offers and uniqueness of the stationary outcome. Do not claim this classifies every possible history-dependent equilibrium.

Check alpha=1/3,delta=1/2,s=3/4, including the gain from immediate agreement relative to a rejection for either proposer. Compare common discounting with unequal patience. Finally set delta=exp(-r*h),s=exp(-v*h), where r,v>0 are impatience rates and h>0 is time between offers. Derive the allocation limit as h approaches0, including whether the realized division still depends on who proposes.

offers_by_proposer: s*(1 - alpha)*(1 - delta)/(alpha*(1 - s) + (1 - alpha)*(1 - delta))

problem:
Help me check this monopoly tax calculation. I used the linear-demand rule that monopoly sells half the efficient quantity, but the demand here has a square root. Is the rule still valid?

A quantity-setting monopolist faces inverse demand p(q)=3-sqrt(q) on0<=q<=9. Real production cost is q. A unit tax alpha, permitted in[-1,infinity), is paid to the government; negative alpha is a subsidy. The firm's profit is[p(q)-1-alpha]*q. There are no fixed costs. Positive revenue is rebated lump sum to consumers; a subsidy is financed by a lump-sum consumer charge. These payments do not affect demand or marginal incentives and have no collection cost. Gross consumer benefit is the integral of inverse demand from0 to q, and total real welfare subtracts production cost only.

Derive the globally optimal monopoly quantity and profit for every alpha, including shutdown. Give the sold price and tax pass-through when output is positive. Find efficient output and the tax or subsidy implementing it. At alpha=0,1/2,-1 calculate output, sold price, profit, consumer surplus before the lump-sum transfer, government revenue and total real welfare. Explain why subsidy spending must not be subtracted twice, verify the ledger against gross benefit, and compute the untaxed monopoly's welfare ratio to efficiency. Use an analytic change of variable where useful, not a search over quantities.

Peux-tu vérifier mon raisonnement? J'ai maximisé chaque morceau du profit et je pense qu'il existe forcément un meilleur prix. Mais la frange concurrentielle se met à produire d'un coup.

La demande est D(p)=4-p pour p dans[0,4]. Une entreprise dominante à coût marginal nul choisit ce prix et sert la demande résiduelle. La frange a capacité K dans[0,3] et coût réel CF(qF)=qF pour0<=qF<=K. Sa règle d'offre est qF=0 si p<1 et qF=K si p>=1: à l'indifférence p=1, elle utilise toute sa capacité. Seuls les prix avec D(p)>=qF sont réalisables, et qD=D(p)-qF. Le profit dominant est p*qD. Il n'y a ni coût d'installation ni autre règle de rationnement. Le bénéfice brut est4*Q-Q^2/2 et le bien-être réel retranche uniquement CF. Un planificateur peut utiliser librement la technologie dominante sans coût.

Caractérise pour chaque K tous les prix globalement optimaux, ou le supremum de profit si aucun prix optimal n'existe. Identifie exactement le seuil de capacité et son cas d'égalité. Si le supremum n'est pas atteint, une randomisation des prix peut-elle l'atteindre? Construis un prix dont le profit soit à epsilon du supremum pour0<epsilon<=1. Donne le bien-être des optima existants, sa limite le long des prix approchant le supremum, et explique pourquoi il serait trompeur de présenter cette limite comme le bien-être d'un équilibre atteint. Vérifie K=1 avec p=9/10 par un compte direct.

Kannst du mir erklären, warum das Medianwählertheorem hier nicht hilft? Jeder hat doch eine einzige ideale Politik. Ich möchte einen Beweis für die ganze Ebene und keine Suche über viele Politikpunkte.

Drei Wähler haben Idealpunkte a1=(0,0),a2=(2,0),a3=(0,2). Jede Politik x ist in der gesamten Ebene R^2 zulässig. Nutzen ist ui(x)=-||x-ai||^2. In einer paarweisen Abstimmung gewinnt y gegen x, wenn mindestens zwei Wähler y strikt vorziehen. Ein Condorcet-Sieger wird von keiner anderen Politik auf diese Weise geschlagen. Es gibt keine Transfers.

Beweise allgemein für diese drei Idealpunkte, dass kein Condorcet-Sieger existiert. Verwende die Projektion eines Politikpunkts auf das Verbindungssegment zweier Idealpunkte, und begründe die strikte Verbesserung für beide Wähler. Prüfe den Mehrheitszyklus zwischen A=(0,0),B=(1,1),C=(0,1). Finde außerdem die Politik mit maximaler Nutzensumme, eine explizite mehrheitlich bevorzugte Alternative dazu, und deren genaue zusätzliche Gesamtverlustkosten. Erkläre den Unterschied zwischen einem eindimensionalen Idealpunktargument, Pareto-Verbesserung und Mehrheitsverbesserung.

Can you help me interpret this encouragement experiment? The instrumental-variable estimate is positive, but does it tell me how many people benefit, or the average effect for everyone? Please derive what is identified and give sharp bounds for the rest.

A binary randomized encouragement Z is independent of all potential treatment and outcome variables. Treatment is D=D(Z), with D(0),D(1) in{0,1}. Outcomes are binary Y(0),Y(1), with observed Y=Y(D); encouragement has no direct effect on outcome. Maintain treatment monotonicity D(1)>=D(0), allowing always-takers, never-takers and compliers. No assumption of equal effects or individual outcome monotonicity is imposed initially.

Conditional on Z=0, the joint probabilities of(D,Y) are D0,Y0:11/20; D0,Y1:1/5; D1,Y0:1/20; D1,Y1:1/5. Conditional on Z=1 they are D0,Y0:1/5; D0,Y1:1/20; D1,Y0:1/5; D1,Y1:11/20. These are exact population probabilities, not noisy sample frequencies.

Identify the three treatment-type shares, the first stage, reduced-form outcome effect and Wald ratio. Use the full joint tables to identify the compliers' two outcome means and the observed potential-outcome means for the other types. Find the sharp identified set for the population average treatment effect. Then find the sharp range of the fraction of compliers who individually benefit, parameterizing their entire potential-outcome joint table with t=P(Y(0)=1,Y(1)=1|complier). Prove attainability without listing all latent response patterns. Finally add Y(1)>=Y(0) for every person: determine the revised average-effect interval and complier benefit fraction. Explain which conclusions use this additional assumption.

Peux-tu vérifier cette affirmation du cours: les optima d'une fonction rawlsienne seraient nécessairement efficaces au sens de Pareto? Je ne vois pas ce qui arrive lorsque la personne la moins favorisée ne peut plus gagner d'utilité.

Une unité de ressource peut être répartie en x,y>=0 avec x+y<=1. Les utilités sont u1=min(x,1/3),u2=y: la première personne est satisfaite à partir de1/3 de ressource, sans autre utilité des unités supplémentaires. Le critère rawlsien est R=min(u1,u2), le critère utilitariste B=u1+u2. La dominance de Pareto signifie des utilités toutes faiblement supérieures et au moins une strictement supérieure.

Trouve l'ensemble complet des allocations Pareto-efficaces, tous les maximisateurs de R et de B, et leurs valeurs. Donne deux allocations utilisant toute la ressource qui maximisent R, dont l'une domine strictement l'autre au sens de Pareto. Ajoute ensuite un départage lexicographique: parmi les maximisateurs de R, maximise B. Compare avec R+epsilon*B pour tout epsilon>0. Prouve les optima globaux par des bornes, sans chercher des allocations sur une grille. Explique enfin quelle propriété d'une fonction de bien-être garantit que chacun de ses maximisateurs est Pareto-efficace, et pourquoi une simple monotonie faible ne suffit pas.

Help me understand the difference between an action and a strategy. Each player can choose0 or1, but someone gave each player four pure strategies such as "choose the opposite of the other player's action". Can I really use that rule when I cannot see the action?

Player1 receives payoff1 when the two actions match and-1 when they differ. Player2 receives the negative of that payoff. All payoffs and rules are common knowledge. Compare three games: simultaneous choices; player1 chooses first and player2 observes the choice; player1 chooses first but player2 does not observe it, with its two possible decision nodes in a single information set. Randomizations in the simultaneous and unobserved games are private and independent; there is no mediator or common random signal.

Give the number of pure strategies for each player in each game, without listing all strategy combinations. Derive all equilibrium results: Nash for simultaneous and unobserved play, subgame-perfect for observed play. For mixing probabilities r=P(a1=1),s=P(a2=1), derive the unobserved expected payoff and prove the equilibrium analytically. Explain which games have complete information and which have perfect information under their extensive-form representation. Finally distinguish an observed response map from an infeasible rule conditioning on unseen actions, and say why reversing the sequential order while revealing the first action transfers the advantage to the new second mover.

Can you help me check a Coase-style claim? Producers and the pollution victim can bargain freely, so someone says their agreement must be socially efficient. But consumers do not participate in their bargain.

Aggregate consumer benefit is U(q)=2*q-q^2/2, industry real production cost C(q)=q^2/2, and victim damage H(q)=q, with0<=q<=2. Without a contract the industry is competitive, with market price equating marginal benefit and marginal production cost. The resulting producer profit, consumer surplus and victim payoff define disagreement values. The victim cannot otherwise change that competitive allocation.

A binding agreement may set an industry-wide aggregate output quota q. If agreed, consumers buy that output at the market-clearing inverse demand p=2-q; aggregate producer profit before transfers is p*q-C(q). Producers cannot unilaterally form or change a quota without this agreement. The victim pays a transfer T>=0 to the producer association. Only producers and the victim negotiate initially. Their stipulated choice maximizes the product of their nonnegative gains over competitive disagreement; bargaining is fully informed, enforceable and has no real transaction cost or wealth constraint. Consumers receive no transfer in this two-party contract.

Derive competitive output and all disagreement payoffs, efficient output and a Pigouvian unit-tax benchmark with receipts rebated lump sum. Solve the two-party contract globally and give its output, transfer, gains, consumer loss and welfare gap to efficiency. Then allow consumers to join: all three parties maximize the product of their nonnegative disagreement gains with unrestricted balanced monetary transfers and the same quota technology. Solve that outcome and give one implementing set of transfers. Prove why adding the missing stakeholder changes the output rather than merely distributing the same surplus. This is a declared contracting institution, not an assertion that one competitive firm can independently choose aggregate market output.

Can you check this claim about utility units? Squaring nonnegative payoffs keeps their order, so someone says it cannot change a mixed-strategy equilibrium. I want to see the exact calculation and the missing assumption.

Two players choose simultaneously. Player1 chooses U or D; player2 chooses L or R. Player1's payoff matrix, with rows U,D and columns L,R, is [[4,0],[1,2]]. Player2's is [[0,2],[3,1]]. Players maximize expected payoff and use private independent randomization. Let r=P(U),s=P(L).

Find all pure and mixed Nash equilibria and equilibrium expected payoffs. Then replace only player1's payoff at every pure outcome by its square, keeping player2's matrix unchanged and again maximizing expected transformed payoff. Recompute equilibria and check directly whether the original mixed profile remains an equilibrium. Compare with replacing player1's payoff by3*u+5. Distinguish an ordinal relabeling of deterministic outcomes from changing preferences over lotteries.

Finally, suppose a strictly increasing function f on[0,4] is required to preserve every indifference between any finite lottery of original utility levels and the certain utility level equal to its original expectation. Show why f must be positive affine on that interval using only a lottery between0 and4. Explain why applying f to the expected payoff is different from taking the expectation of transformed outcome payoffs.

Je pensais que deux laboratoires qui cherchent en parallèle avaient forcément plus de chances de trouver qu'un seul. Peux-tu vérifier cette intuition quand chacun choisit aussi son effort ? Je veux comprendre le mécanisme, pas essayer une liste d'investissements.

Deux entreprises choisissent simultanément xi dans[0,1]. Le coût réel de recherche est3*xi^2/8. Conditionnellement aux investissements, les succès sont indépendants, avec probabilité xi pour l'entreprise i. Une innovation suffit. Si une seule réussit, elle reçoit une récompense monétaire1; si les deux réussissent, une pièce équitable attribue cette unique récompense à l'une d'elles; si aucune ne réussit, aucune récompense n'est versée. Les entreprises sont neutres au risque. Un sponsor extérieur finance la récompense par un transfert sans coût de collecte. Le bénéfice réel pour la société est2 lorsqu'au moins une entreprise réussit, zéro sinon. Les coûts de recherche sont toujours payés.

Trouve l'unique équilibre de recherche non coopératif, sa probabilité de découverte, les profits nets individuels et le surplus réel, sponsor inclus. Un accord contraignant choisit les investissements pour maximiser la somme des profits nets; trouve tous ses optima globaux, puis ceux du planificateur social. Explique pourquoi chercher un optimum symétrique peut échouer. Compare probabilité de découverte, dépenses et bien-être; donne une décomposition exacte de la perte non coopérative.

Une pièce publique peut choisir avant les efforts quelle entreprise sera l'unique chercheuse. Calcule les profits espérés de ce partage des rôles, mais vérifie si l'entreprise désignée inactive voudrait dévier en l'absence d'accord contraignant. Enfin, une taxe commune tau>=0 par unité de xi peut-elle faire de(1,0) un équilibre ? Les recettes sont des transferts. Compare avec des taxes ciblées(0,1/2).

Kannst du mir helfen, diese Vorhersagegarantie richtig zu verstehen? Mein Intervall trifft insgesamt75 Prozent der Fälle. Darf ich deshalb auch für jede Bevölkerungsgruppe und nach Beobachtung meiner Kalibrierungsdaten75 Prozent versprechen?

Ein Prognosemodell m ist vor der Kalibrierung festgelegt und wird danach nicht verändert. Für eine neue Person lautet das Vorhersageintervall[m(X)-R,m(X)+R]. Sein Fehlermaß ist E=|Y-m(X)|. Drei Kalibrierungspersonen und die neue Person sind unabhängig aus derselben Population gezogen. Jede gehört mit Wahrscheinlichkeit1/2 zur Gruppe A oder B. Bedingt auf A ist E gleichverteilt auf[0,1], bedingt auf B auf[1,2]. Es gibt keine weiteren Abhängigkeiten. Die gepoolte Regel setzt R=max(E1,E2,E3).

Beweise zunächst die marginale Überdeckungswahrscheinlichkeit durch Austauschbarkeit der vier stetigen Fehler, ohne Simulation. Berechne sie unabhängig über die Verteilung von R. Bestimme außerdem die Überdeckung bedingt auf die Gruppe der neuen Person, jeweils gemittelt über die Kalibrierungsdaten. Berechne die Überdeckung bedingt auf R=r. Wenn alle drei Kalibrierungspersonen aus A kommen: Wie wahrscheinlich ist dieses Ereignis, und welche Überdeckung erhält die neue Person dann insgesamt und in jeder Gruppe?

Eine zweite Methode sammelt genau drei unabhängige Kalibrierungsfehler pro Gruppe und verwendet für die neue Person das Maximum ihrer eigenen Gruppe. Berechne die gruppenspezifischen Überdeckungen. Diese Methode benutzt sechs statt drei Kalibrierungspersonen; verschweige diesen Unterschied nicht.

Zum Schluss bleiben wir bei den ursprünglichen drei zufällig gezogenen Kalibrierungspersonen. Innerhalb jeder Gruppe seien M die Anzahl ihrer Kalibrierungsfehler und k=ceil(3*(M+1)/4). Die gruppenspezifische Regel nimmt den k-ten kleinsten Fehler, ergänzt aber ein zusätzliches +unendlich und verwendet dieses, falls k=M+1. Bestimme für M=0,1,2,3 die Schwellenart sowie die Überdeckung für eine neue Person aus jeder Gruppe. Erkläre, welche Garantie gültig ist und welche bedingte Garantie daraus nicht folgt.

How can I solve this matching problem without listing every possible assignment? I also cannot see why a unique efficient allocation would leave wages undetermined.

There are three workers with skills a=(1,2,4) and three firms with technologies b=(1,3,5). Each worker can work for at most one firm and each firm can employ at most one worker. Matching worker i to firm j produces a_i*b_j units of the numeraire. A wage transfers output from firm to worker; there are no other costs or taxes. Unmatched workers and firms get0. A stable competitive outcome is individually rational and has no blocking worker-firm pair: no pair can rematch and split its output so that both strictly improve. All matched output is split between wage w_i and the corresponding firm's profit.

Find the unique efficient matching without enumerating assignments. Characterize every stable wage and profit vector, not just one. Give the componentwise worker-best and firm-best stable outcomes. Someone proposes to give each worker the same fraction theta in[0,1] of their matched output. Find exactly which fractions are stable. If theta=1/3 is unstable, exhibit a blocking pair and a wage that benefits both equally.

Now raise the third firm's technology from5 to7, with all other assumptions unchanged. Find the new efficient output and stable wage set. Compare the shock's incidence at the worker-best and firm-best stable outcomes. Explain which statements about allocation and income distribution the competitive model actually identifies.

Help me understand this apparent contradiction: two goods become nearly identical, yet a tiny price difference can radically change which one the consumer buys. Does utility also explode, or am I using the demand formula outside its valid range?

The consumer maximizes U=4*(q1+q2)-(q1^2+2*alpha*q1*q2+q2^2)/2+y, with q1,q2,y>=0 and budget(1+epsilon)*q1+(1-epsilon)*q2+y<=100. Assume0<=alpha<1 and0<=epsilon<=1/2. Prices are p1=1+epsilon,p2=1-epsilon. Find the complete demand, including the switching condition and any corner. Prove global optimality and show the numeraire remains positive.

At alpha=9/10,epsilon=1/10 and at alpha=99/100,epsilon=1/10, give exact quantities. Then set alpha=1 separately: find the entire demand set when epsilon=0 and the demand when epsilon>0. Explain which part of an equal-split convention is a choice rather than a consequence of optimization.

Compare the two iterated limits as epsilon tends to0 from above and alpha tends to1 from below. More generally, along epsilon=lambda*(1-alpha), lambda>=0 fixed, find the limiting allocation and give it for lambda=0,1,2. Derive the interior sensitivity of quantities to epsilon and the eigenvalue condition number of the curvature matrix. Finally, compute maximal utility minus100 on the interior and corner branches and its limit along those scaled-price paths. Do not extend a negative unconstrained quantity into a demand answer.

Je ne comprends pas: on me dit qu'un impôt forfaitaire ne crée pas de distorsion, mais dans mon calcul il augmente le travail. Est-ce une contradiction ? Peux-tu aussi vérifier pourquoi deux taux d'impôt peuvent rapporter exactement la même recette ?

Un ménage dispose d'une unité de temps. Il choisit un travail L dans[0,1] et une consommation c>=0; son loisir est1-L et son utilité U=c*(1-L). Le salaire brut par unité de travail est4 et le revenu non salarial est1. Le salaire est exogène. Il n'y a ni épargne ni autre marché. Le gouvernement finance une même dépense fixée G=1/4, sans frais de collecte; son éventuel bénéfice pour le ménage est identique sous toutes les politiques et omis de U.

Sous un impôt proportionnel tau dans[0,1] sur le salaire, la contrainte est c<=1+4*(1-tau)*L et la recette R=tau*4*L. Sous un impôt forfaitaire F=1/4, elle est c<=1+4*L-F. Le ménage prend l'impôt comme donné; il ne considère pas sa recette individuelle comme un remboursement qui dépend de son choix.

Trouve l'offre de travail globale sous l'impôt proportionnel, y compris l'arrêt du travail, et la fonction de recette. Trouve son maximum et tous les taux finançant G exactement. Pour chaque taux, donne travail, consommation, loisir et utilité, puis compare au régime forfaitaire et à l'absence d'impôt. Explique pourquoi le forfait peut modifier le travail tout en conservant le prix relatif privé égal au prix relatif réel. Prouve l'ordre de bien-être pour une recette donnée par un carré sur la contrainte de ressources; ne compare pas seulement les taux ou une dérivée locale.

Can you check my bootstrap argument? I have observations from a uniform distribution with an unknown upper endpoint. I resampled the observations and used bootstrap percentiles of the sample maximum as a confidence interval for that endpoint. Why might increasing the number of bootstrap repetitions fail to fix this?

Let X1,...,Xn be independent Uniform[0,v], with unknown v>0 and integer n>=1. Set M=max(X1,...,Xn). An ordinary nonparametric bootstrap draws n observations independently with replacement from the observed empirical distribution and computes M_star. Conditional on the original data, assume the observed maximum is unique; this holds almost surely. Let r=exp(-1), a declared constant.

Derive the exact distribution of M/v and its first two moments. Give an unbiased endpoint estimator and its variance. Derive the finite-sample CDF of T=n*(v-M)/v on[0,n] and its limiting distribution. For the bootstrap analogue T_star=n*(M-M_star)/M, calculate exactly the conditional probability T_star=0 and its limit. Use this to prove that the ordinary bootstrap does not reproduce the sampling law of this scaled endpoint error.

For the concrete observed sample(1,2,3), with n=3, compute the bootstrap probabilities of M_star=1,2,3, its conditional mean and variance, and the conditional bootstrap bias estimate for M. Explain why any percentile-only interval whose upper endpoint is a bootstrap quantile of M_star has zero coverage for v in this continuous model.

As a model-based alternative, generate n fresh Uniform[0,M] observations and their maximum M_param. Compare the exact conditional law of n*(M-M_param)/M to T. Derive a confidence interval for v with exact coverage7/8 when n=3, and evaluate it for the concrete sample. Distinguish an exact pivot under the uniform model from a distribution-free bootstrap claim. No simulation or listing of all resampled sequences.

Je ne sais pas comment résoudre ce consommateur: la matrice de demande est singulière. On me dit aussi que des compléments parfaits doivent être consommés dans les mêmes proportions. Est-ce vraiment vrai pour cette utilité quadratique ?

Le consommateur maximise U=4*(q1+q2)-(q1-q2)^2/2+y, avec q1,q2,y>=0 et budget q1+3*q2+y<=r, où r>=0. Le bien composite y est le numéraire. Les prix des deux biens sont1 et3. La fonction donnée est utilisée telle quelle: ne remplace pas sa partie quadratique par une utilité de Leontief et n'applique pas une inversion singulière.

Trouve la demande complète pour tous les revenus r, le seuil d'entrée du bien2, la valeur maximale et sa dérivée pour r>0. Prouve l'optimalité globale et l'unicité malgré la courbure nulle dans une direction. Pour r=1 puis r=10, donne les quantités, y et la valeur. Au revenu10, vérifie les conditions marginales avec le multiplicateur du budget et compare avec un panier équilibré q1=q2.

Explique exactement pourquoi l'équilibre peut garder un écart de quantités constant alors que leur ratio dépend du revenu. Une affirmation prétend que, dans ce modèle symétrique, le bien plus cher pourrait être consommé en quantité strictement plus grande à un optimum intérieur. Teste-la par les conditions marginales à prix positifs. Enfin, que se passe-t-il si on autorise y à devenir négatif sans limite ?

My simulated action frequencies are uniform and neither player benefits from switching permanently to one action. Is that enough to call the recommendations a correlated equilibrium? Please help me check the conditional incentives exactly.

Two players choose R,P,S. Player1's payoff matrix, with its actions as rows and player2's actions as columns in that order, is A=[[0,-1,1],[1,0,-1],[-1,1,0]]. Player2 gets the negative of A. A mediator draws an ordered action pair and privately recommends each player's own action. Consider the law assigning probability1/6 to each unequal-action pair and zero to equal-action pairs. Each player observes only their own recommendation.

A coarse correlated equilibrium permits deviations selected before seeing the recommendation: a fixed action or independently randomized action instead of obedience. A correlated equilibrium also permits a player to condition the deviation on their own observed recommendation. Use these definitions as given.

Compute the recommended payoffs, marginals and best fixed-deviation payoff. For each possible recommendation, find the best conditional deviation and its conditional gain; give a single recommendation-dependent rule and its overall gain. Decide whether the proposed law is coarse correlated, correlated or an independently mixed Nash profile.

Go beyond this one example: characterize every coarse correlated law by its marginals and expected payoff, and prove that the unique correlated law for this particular game is the independent uniform law. Prove the unique mixed Nash profile too. Your proof should use zero-sum security and nonnegative incentive gaps, not try probability tables one at a time. Explain why aggregate no-fixed-deviation checks miss the flaw.

Which of these two information sources should I buy? One has a better average probability forecast, but I care about a decision with an asymmetric loss. Can the better forecast still be the worse signal for my decision?

The unknown state is H or L with prior probabilities1/2 each. Experiment A returns + or - with likelihood matrix[[3/4,1/4],[1/4,3/4]], rows H,L and columns +,-. Experiment B has matrix[[1/2,1/2],[0,1]]. Both are independent of anything else given the state, and only one experiment is observed. A signal can be garbled into another by applying a state-independent randomized map to its observed + or - output; the map's probabilities must lie in[0,1].

First compute the signal probabilities and posterior probability p=P(H|signal). Under squared error for predicting the state indicator, find the optimal prediction, expected risk and posterior variance for each experiment. Then consider an action paying1 in H and losing k>=0 in L, versus doing nothing with payoff0. Give the optimal expected payoff without a signal and with each experiment as a complete function of k. Locate exactly where A is better, where B is better and where they tie; treat decision indifference at the threshold correctly.

At k=1/2 and k=2, give each experiment's maximum worthwhile fee relative to no signal, assuming the fee is paid before observation and does not change the action's payoffs. Finally, test whether either experiment is a garbling of the other by solving for the two output-map probabilities. Relate the result to the crossing decision values. Do not rank experiments by accuracy or posterior variance alone.

I thought Rawls meant choosing the best equal split. Can you explain why an equal-payoff point might be dominated while the max-min point is unequal? Please prove it from the feasible set, rather than relying on the look of a diagram.

Two persons have feasible utility pairs in K={(x,y):x>=0,y>=0,(x-2)^2+(y-5)^2<=5}. These utility numbers and their cardinal scales are fixed. There is initially no technology for discarding one person's utility while preserving the other's, and no transfers beyond what K already permits. Pareto efficiency means no feasible pair raises at least one utility without lowering the other.

Find the full Pareto-efficient frontier. Find the Bentham maximum of x+y and the Rawls maximum of min(x,y), including all maximizing pairs. Also find every feasible equal-utility pair and the equal-utility pair with largest common value. Test whether that egalitarian choice is Pareto efficient by giving an explicit dominating pair. Do not confuse the equality constraint x=y with the max-min objective.

Now add free utility disposal: the feasible set becomes D={(a,b):a,b>=0 and there is some(x,y) in K with a<=x,b<=y}. Compute the Rawls maximizing set and best equal-utility pair in D, identify which Rawls maximizers are Pareto efficient, and determine whether the Bentham optimum changes. Explain which results depend on the initial absence of disposal, and whether adding disposal creates any larger total welfare.

How should I design deterrence when I know the two event probabilities but not their dependence? I was going to multiply the marginals. Please check whether that gives a robust policy and whether a penalty cap changes the answer.

An action gives a risk-neutral firm gain1/2. The authority chooses an investigation probability a in[0,1] and flat penalty F>=0. Let I indicate investigation. Let C be a latent adjudication outcome: whether the case would satisfy the sanction criterion if considered. Its unconditional probability is3/4, not the probability conditional on I=1. Only the joint event I=C=1 triggers the penalty. The authority knows P(I=1)=a and P(C=1)=3/4 but allows every joint law with these marginals. There is no gain confiscation: the firm's expected incremental gain is1/2-F*P(I=C=1).

The authority seeks weak deterrence, meaning incremental gain<=0 for every admissible joint law. At equality the firm is indifferent; do not assert strict deterrence. The committed real design cost is J=a^2+F^2/32, separately from penalty transfers. First find the least-cost robust policy without a penalty cap. Prove the sharp joint-probability bound by constructing an attaining table, and prove the policy's global optimality without testing many policies.

Now impose F<=v, with v>0. Classify feasibility and all cost-minimizing policies for every v; give the exact optimum and cost at v=1. Finally solve the uncapped design that would result from falsely imposing independence. Calculate its actual worst-case firm gain and decide whether it deters robustly. Explain why a conditional sanction probability would justify a probability product, while the unconditional marginal given here does not.

Mon contrôle synthétique reproduit exactement les deux périodes avant traitement. Est-ce une preuve que son effet estimé est correct ? Peux-tu montrer ce qui est identifié par l'ajustement et ce qu'une pénalisation choisit simplement parmi plusieurs possibilités ?

Les résultats sans traitement suivent exactement un modèle à deux facteurs constants dans leurs chargements: Y_it(0)=lambda_i1*f_t1+lambda_i2*f_t2. Il n'y a ni bruit, ni effet du traitement sur les unités témoins, ni anticipation. Le témoin A a chargement(1,0), le témoin B(0,1). L'unité traitée a chargement inconnu(s,1-s), avec0<=s<=1.

Les deux périodes avant traitement ont facteurs(1,1) et(3,3). Les résultats des trois unités sont donc respectivement1 puis3. À la période après traitement, les facteurs sont(2,0): les témoins donnent2 et0.
